---
name: mathlib-conventions
description: Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
---

Write Lean that looks like it belongs in mathlib: discoverable, reusable, and
composing with the existing API. This is the style side; use [[leansearch]] to
*find* lemmas and [[lean-check]] to verify, and keep the blueprint in step via
[[blueprint-conventions]].

## Naming

- **Theorems / lemmas / `Prop`s → `snake_case`**, named by *what the statement
  says*, composing the pieces in order: `add_comm`, `mul_le_mul_left`,
  `isOpen_iUnion`, `continuous_id`. A reader should reconstruct the statement
  from the name.
- **Types, structures, classes, inductives → `UpperCamelCase`**: `LinearMap`,
  `IsLindelof`, `RiemannianMetric`.
- **Definitions / terms / functions → `lowerCamelCase`**: `leviCivita`,
  `koszulRHS`, `parallelTransport`.
- **Structural predicates take the `Is` prefix**: `IsOpen`, `IsCompact`,
  `IsSymmetric`.
- **Name order relations by the operator you wrote**, not its mirror: use `le`
  / `lt` (`le_of_lt`, `add_lt_add`), not `ge` / `gt`.
- **Meaningful names only.** No `helper1`, `foo_aux`, `my_lemma`, `lemma2`.
  Ad-hoc names are invisible to search and un-reusable — the whole point of a
  mathlib-style name is that the next session (or mathlib itself) can find it.

## Search before you prove, prefer before you build

- Your "obvious lemma" is very likely already in mathlib under a more general
  name. Search first ([[leansearch]]); a negative result after a precise query
  means it's genuinely absent — then prove it, don't keep rephrasing.
- **Choose the reusable abstraction**, so your work composes with mathlib rather
  than sitting in a private silo: `Filter`/`Tendsto` over hand-rolled ε–δ, the
  Bochner `MeasureTheory.integral` over an ad-hoc integral, bundled morphisms
  (`…Hom`) and typeclasses over unbundled functions-plus-hypotheses, unless the
  problem is genuinely about the lower-level object.

## Missing infrastructure → build it properly, don't defer or hack

When a needed fact truly isn't in mathlib, the failure mode is to leave a
`sorry` "waiting for an upstream PR", or to inline a brittle one-off. Instead:

- **State the missing lemma in mathlib-ready generality**, with a proper name and
  a *real* proof attempt (a partial proof beats a documented gap), as
  project-local infrastructure others can reuse.
- **Factor hard steps into their own named, reusable lemmas** rather than a
  monolithic proof — mirroring the blueprint's "split, don't abbreviate" rule.
- **Record it** so it isn't an invisible dependency: give the new declaration a
  blueprint node (`\lean{…}` + `\uses{…}`) and note it for the roadmap, so future
  sessions and the DAG can see the new frontier ([[blueprint-conventions]], [[hgraph]]).

## House style (light touch)

- Module docstring at the top; group related material into `section`s /
  `namespace`s; keep lines readable (~100 cols); align `calc` steps.
- Prefer `simp`/`grind`-normal statements so lemmas fire as `@[simp]` candidates
  and rewrites compose.
- Comments explain the *mathematics*, not the development history ("was a sorry",
  "TODO next session" — keep that in the report/inbox, not the source).
- Mark reusable facts `@[simp]` only when they're genuinely confluent rewrites.

## Faithfulness (non-negotiable)

- **Never weaken a statement to make it pass**, and never change a declaration's
  statement to dodge its proof. A proof that games the checker is a failure.
- **No `axiom` / `admit` / `native_decide` on a goal you haven't honestly
  closed**, and no `sorry` reported as done — see [[lean-check]] for verifying a
  build is genuinely sorry-free.

---
name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

Read in this order before editing:

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Operational
messages are deltas, not reports. Default to one sentence or at most three short
bullets covering conclusion, new evidence, and next action; do not repeat the
thread, commit diff, or session history. Use headings only when a genuinely
multi-part decision needs them. Agent comments target at most 600 characters and
are rejected above 1200; descriptions/opening messages target 800 and are
rejected above 2400. Humans are not subject to these bounds.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

### Conversation lifecycle

A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.

1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
   open one thread per incremental finding.
2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
   team.
4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
   warning says the inbox is full.
5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what changed; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the body; authorship is automatic. Comment only at a **key advance** such
  as a milestone, ruled-out route, blocker, correction, or conclusion. Update the
  existing thread with the delta instead of re-establishing its full context.
- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body "Topic\n\nOpening message"`
  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live
  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a
  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other
  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.
- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
  For a conversation you initiated, this is the normal "discussion finished"
  operation after its answer/conclusion has been consumed.
- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
  — open a new item.
  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct
    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.
    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it"); use `--to task:<id>` to
    message a specific running team.
  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
    the shared default.
  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
    tag to the body.
  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.

Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
modified.

---
name: leansearch
description: Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
---

**Search before you prove.** Most facts you need already exist in mathlib or the
workspace. Searching is far cheaper than reproving. Use the local index first
(unlimited, instant), then the LSP search tools for broader semantic/type search.

## Local first: `horizon search`

An offline declaration search over `external_libraries` (mathlib by default) plus
the workspace's own projects. No GPU, API key, or network. Three modes share one
cached index:

- Natural language — what a lemma says:
  `horizon search "continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum"`
- `--name` — find a declaration by partial name:
  `horizon search --name isCompact.image`
- `--type` — find by shape of the statement; `?a`/`?b`/`_` are wildcards:
  `horizon search --type "Continuous ?f -> IsCompact ?s -> IsCompact (?f '' ?s)"`

Useful flags: `-n K`, `--lib NAME`, `--json`, `--reindex`. If results look thin,
run the project build so sources are current, then `horizon search --reindex`.

## Lean LSP MCP search tools

The `lean-lsp` MCP server (configured in `.mcp.json`) exposes a full search
arsenal. Rate limits are **per-tool** (separate pools), not a shared budget.

| Tool | Use it for | Limit |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `lean_local_search` | exact/partial declaration name; workspace + mathlib | unlimited |
| `lean_leansearch` | **semantic search by mathematical meaning** (PKU LeanSearch) | 10 / 30s |
| `lean_loogle` | search by **type shape** when you know the signature, not the name | remote; unlimited in `--loogle-local` |
| `lean_state_search` | lemmas that apply to a specific **proof state** (goal at a line) | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_hammer_premise` | **premise names** to feed `simp only [...]` / `aesop` / `grind` | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_leanfinder` | semantic fallback — only when `lean_leansearch` fails | 10 / 30s |

### Priority / escalation order

1. `lean_local_search("name")` — always first; unlimited, instant, deterministic.
2. `lean_leansearch("describe the math.")` — primary semantic search (see below).
3. `lean_loogle("?a -> ?b")` — simple type patterns only.
4. `lean_state_search(file, line, col)` — goal-conditioned lookup when stuck.
5. `lean_hammer_premise(file, line, col)` — premises for `simp`/`aesop`/`grind`.
6. `lean_leanfinder("description")` — last-resort semantic fallback.

### `lean_leansearch` — the PKU semantic tool (use it well)

LeanSearch (leansearch.net, from the PKU team) augments each mathlib theorem into
an informal description and matches your query against those embeddings —
returning the **nearest neighbours**, not just exact hits. That is its strength:
a theorem 90% of what you need is often enough; prove the small gap yourself.

- **Describe the mathematical content, not the name.** Query must end with `.`/`?`.
  - Good: `lean_leansearch("The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.")`
  - Good (mixed): `lean_leansearch("natural numbers. from: n < m, to: n + 1 < m + 1")`
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("add_comm")` → use `lean_local_search` instead.
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("∀ (a b : ℕ), a + b = b + a")` → use `lean_loogle` instead.
- **Trust a negative result.** If a precise, mathematically accurate description
  returns nothing relevant, the theorem likely isn't in mathlib — stop rephrasing
  and prove it (or find another route) rather than searching endlessly.

### `lean_loogle` — type-shape search

Searches by *type structure*, not names. Syntax: `?a`/`?b` type vars, `_`
wildcards, `->`/`→` arrows, `|- pattern` by conclusion.
- Good: `lean_loogle("(?a -> ?b) -> List ?a -> List ?b")` → `List.map`
- Anti-pattern: nested `Submodule`/`LinearMap`/`Finsupp`, 3+ typeclass
  constraints, or guessy implicit structure — use `lean_leansearch` for those.

## Discipline

- Treat every hit as a **candidate**: read the signature/source and confirm with
  the Lean checker (see the `lean-check` skill) before depending on it.
- Try multiple phrasings — project name, mathematical concept, conclusion/type.
- Local (`horizon search` / `lean_local_search`) is optimized for the checked-out
  sources here; the LSP tools reach broader mathlib precedent. Use both.

name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

   286	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCert.lean` (`toOvlLeft_mk'`/`toOvlRight_mk'`) — and both are `rfl`,
   287	so this is a name, not a proof (inbox `I-0712`: `private` hides the name, not the argument).
   288	The `resHom` spelling is the one the matching law below rewrites along. -/
   289	lemma toOvlLeft_mk (i j : D.index) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i)) :
   290	    A.toOvlLeft i j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn i}) s)
   291	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j)
   292	          ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left s) :=
   293	  rfl

   295	/-- The right overlap arrow on a residue class. -/
   296	lemma toOvlRight_mk (i j : D.index) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)) :
   297	    A.toOvlRight i j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) s)
   298	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j)
   299	          ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right s) :=
   300	  rfl
   301	
   302	/-- **The evaluation lands in the widened Θ-twisted glued module**: on each pairwise
   303	overlap, the global matching of the two side components through the theta cocycle *is* the
   304	Θ-twisted matching of the colengths.
   305	
   306	Where the chart-typed proof (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaEval_mem`) runs a four-case `Sum`
   307	split and calls `relThetaSections_matching` twice with hand-built containments, this is a
   308	single application of `relThetaResSide_matching` — the side-uniform form of the same
   309	matching law.  That collapse is the concrete payoff of taking the sides from a
   310	`ChartTyping` rather than from the index type. -/
   311	theorem thetaEval_mem (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   312	    thetaEval A τ a x ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a := by
   313	  rw [mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff]
   314	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
   315	  rw [thetaEval_apply, thetaEval_apply, toOvlLeft_mk, toOvlRight_mk, ← map_mul]
   316	  refine congrArg _ ?_
   317	  -- both sides restrict the SAME section into the overlap; the side matching law compares
   318	  -- the two assigned sides there, and `thetaOvlUnit` is by definition its unit
   319	  rw [resHom_relThetaResSide (b := τ.side i), resHom_relThetaResSide (b := τ.side j)]
   320	  exact relThetaResSide_matching a (τ.side i) (τ.side j)
   321	    (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j) x
   322	
   323	/-- **The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a widened cover.** -/
   324	noncomputable def thetaGluedEval :
   325	    relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] ThetaGlued A τ a :=
   326	  LinearMap.codRestrict (thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a) (thetaEval A τ a) (thetaEval_mem A τ a)

   329	    (thetaGluedEval A τ a x : A.chartProd) = thetaEval A τ a x := rfl

   332	lemma ker_thetaGluedEval_eq_ker :
   333	    LinearMap.ker (thetaGluedEval A τ a) = LinearMap.ker (thetaEval A τ a) :=
   334	  LinearMap.ker_codRestrict _ _ _

   336	/-! ## The equalizer algebra and the unit-twisted glued modules
   337	
   338	Everything in this section is **cover-generic**: it names `D.pieces`, `A.ovlIdeal`,
   339	`A.toOvlLeft/Right` and nothing about a chart, so it ports from
   340	`Picard/DivisorFamilyThetaRank.lean:77-231` with `AffAdaptation` in place of
   341	`DivisorAdaptation` and no other change.  It is the substrate a widened `IsThetaPaired` —
   342	the honest cohomological residue of the (c2)-transport — is stated over. -/
   343	
   344	/-- **The equalizer algebra `A_D` over a widened cover**: the glued colength module is an
   345	`R`-subalgebra of the piece product, because the overlap-restriction arrows are algebra
   346	maps. -/
   347	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebra : Subalgebra R A.chartProd where
   348	  carrier := A.gluedSubmodule
   349	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => A.gluedSubmodule.add_mem hx hy
   350	  mul_mem' := by
   351	    intro x y hx hy
   352	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff] at hx hy ⊢
   353	    intro p
   354	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, map_mul, hx p, hy p]
   355	  one_mem' := by
   356	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   357	    intro p
   358	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one]
   359	  algebraMap_mem' := by
   360	    intro r
   361	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   362	    intro p
   363	    rw [Pi.algebraMap_apply, Pi.algebraMap_apply, AlgHom.commutes, AlgHom.commutes]
   364	
   365	lemma mem_gluedSubalgebra_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   366	    x ∈ gluedSubalgebra A ↔ x ∈ A.gluedSubmodule :=
   367	  Iff.rfl
   368	
   369	/-- The equalizer algebra and the glued module have the same carrier, `R`-linearly. -/
   370	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraEquiv : ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) ≃ₗ[R] A.Glued where
   371	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   372	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   373	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   374	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
   375	  left_inv _ := rfl
   376	  right_inv _ := rfl
   377	
   378	section UnitTwist
   379	
   380	variable (u v : ∀ i j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ)
   381	
   382	/-- The `u`-twisted right overlap arrow for an arbitrary unit family on the piece
   383	overlaps. -/
   384	noncomputable def unitDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   385	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   386	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   387	        ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   388	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   389	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   390	
   391	/-- The `u`-twisted glued colength module. -/
   392	noncomputable def unitGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   393	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - unitDeltaRight A u)
   394	
   395	/-- The `u`-twisted equalizer description. -/
   396	lemma mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   397	    s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   398	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   399	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   400	            ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   401	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   402	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   403	  simp only [unitGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   404	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, unitDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   405	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   406	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   407	
   408	/-- At the trivial unit family, the twisted glued module is the glued module. -/
   409	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_one : unitGluedSubmodule A 1 = A.gluedSubmodule := by
   410	  ext s
   411	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   412	  refine forall_congr' fun p => ?_
   413	  rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, Units.val_one, map_one, one_mul]
   414	
   415	/-- At the Θ unit family, the twisted glued module is the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` — by `rfl`,
   416	exactly as chart-typed, which is what lets the pairing layer be stated over `thetaOvlUnit`
   417	without a transport. -/
   418	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_thetaOvlUnit :
   419	    unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ a) = thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a :=
   420	  rfl
   421	
   422	variable {u v}
   423	
   424	/-- **Twists multiply**: the componentwise product of a `u`-twisted and a `v`-twisted glued
   425	family is `(u * v)`-twisted. -/
   426	theorem mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule {s t : A.chartProd}
   427	    (hs : s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u) (ht : t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A v) :
   428	    s * t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (u * v) := by
   429	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff] at hs ht ⊢
   430	  intro p
   431	  have h1 : (s * t) p.1 = s p.1 * t p.1 := rfl
   432	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl
   433	  have h3 : (((u * v) p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   434	      Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   435	      = ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   436	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   437	        * ((v p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   438	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)) := rfl
   439	  rw [h1, h2, h3, map_mul, map_mul, map_mul, hs p, ht p]
   440	  ring
   441	
   442	variable (u) in
   443	/-- The `u`-twisted glued module as a module over the equalizer algebra `A_D`. -/
   444	noncomputable def unitGluedOver : Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) A.chartProd where
   445	  carrier := unitGluedSubmodule A u
   446	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => (unitGluedSubmodule A u).add_mem hx hy
   447	  zero_mem' := (unitGluedSubmodule A u).zero_mem
   448	  smul_mem' := by
   449	    intro c x hx
   450	    have hc : (c : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A 1 := by
   451	      rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]
   452	      exact c.2
   453	    have hmul := mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule A hc hx
   454	    rw [one_mul] at hmul
   455	    have hsmul : c • x = (c : A.chartProd) * x := Algebra.smul_def c x
   456	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, hsmul]
   457	    exact hmul
   458	
   459	lemma mem_unitGluedOver_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   460	    x ∈ unitGluedOver A u ↔ x ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u :=

    11	/-!
    12	# Intrinsic theta restrictions on widened divisor-family pieces
    13	
    14	The widened cover of `AffAdaptation` consists of arbitrary affine opens.  It therefore
    15	cannot use a pinned-chart trivialization of the theta cocycle.  Instead, on each piece
    16	`D.pieces j` we choose the affine sections model of the intrinsic cocycle-glued theta
    17	line bundle `(thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf`.  Its sections are an invertible module
    18	over the piece ring.
    19	
    20	Base change along the quotient
    21	`Gamma(D.pieces j) -> A.colength j = Gamma(D.pieces j) / (A.eqn j)` gives the intrinsic
    22	restriction of the theta line bundle to the piece of the finite divisor.  Invertibility
    23	is preserved by this base change.  A widened certificate then makes the colength algebra
    24	finite projective over `R`, so the existing invertible-module transfer gives finite and
    25	projective `R`-modules without any chart typing or additional hypothesis.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	set_option autoImplicit false
    29	
    30	universe u
    31	
    32	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    33	open scoped TensorProduct
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    36	
    37	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    38	
    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    40	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    41	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    42	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    43	
    44	namespace AffAdaptation
    45	
    46	/-- The intrinsic theta sections on the widened affine piece `j`. -/
    47	noncomputable abbrev ThetaPieceSections (_A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    48	    (j : D.index) : Type u :=
    49	  (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf.obj.obj (op (D.pieces j))
    50	
    51	/-- A canonical choice of the finite projective invertible sections model of the
    52	intrinsic theta line bundle on the widened affine piece `j`.  The choice internally
    53	refines the arbitrary piece by basic opens subordinate to the theta cover; it does not
    54	type the piece itself into either pinned chart. -/
    55	noncomputable def thetaPieceSectionsModel (_A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    56	    (thetaChartDatum C R π a).AffineSectionsModel (D.pieces j) :=
    57	  Classical.choice ((thetaChartDatum C R π a).nonempty_affineSectionsModel
    58	    (D.pieces j) (D.isAffineOpen j))
    59	
    60	/-- The piece-ring action on intrinsic theta sections selected by
    61	`thetaPieceSectionsModel`. -/
    62	@[reducible]
    63	noncomputable def thetaPieceSectionsModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    64	    Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    65	  letI : Scheme.QcohOn (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf (D.pieces j) :=
    66	    (A.thetaPieceSectionsModel (π := π) a j).qcoh
    67	  Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf)
    68	    (le_refl (D.pieces j))
    69	
    70	/-- The intrinsic restriction of `O(a Theta)` to the divisor inside the widened piece
    71	`j`: tensor theta sections with the equation quotient `A.colength j`. -/
    72	noncomputable abbrev ThetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    73	    (j : D.index) : Type u :=
    74	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    75	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
    76	  A.colength j ⊗[Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)] A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j
    77	
    78	/-- The intrinsic theta restriction is invertible over the piece-local colength algebra.
    79	This is base-change stability of invertible modules. -/
    80	theorem invertible_thetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    81	    Module.Invertible (A.colength j) (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) := by
    82	  let M := A.thetaPieceSectionsModel (π := π) a j
    83	  letI : Scheme.QcohOn (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf (D.pieces j) := M.qcoh
    84	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    85	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
    86	  haveI : Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
    87	      (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) := M.invertible
    88	  change Module.Invertible (A.colength j)
    89	    (A.colength j ⊗[Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)]
    90	      A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j)
    91	  infer_instance
    92	
    93	/-- Under the existing widened certificate, every intrinsic theta restriction is finite
    94	over the test ring. -/
    95	theorem IsCertified.finite_thetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) {n : ℕ}
    96	    (hc : A.IsCertified n) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    97	    Module.Finite R (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) := by
    98	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    99	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
   100	  haveI : Module.Invertible (A.colength j)
   101	      (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) :=
   102	    A.invertible_thetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j
   103	  haveI : Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := hc.finite_colength j
   104	  exact Module.Invertible.finite_trans (A := A.colength j)
   105	
   106	/-- Under the existing widened certificate, every intrinsic theta restriction is
   107	projective over the test ring. -/
   108	theorem IsCertified.projective_thetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) {n : ℕ}
   109	    (hc : A.IsCertified n) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
   110	    Module.Projective R (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) := by
   111	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
   112	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
   113	  haveI : Module.Invertible (A.colength j)
   114	      (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) :=
   115	    A.invertible_thetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j
   116	  haveI : Module.Projective R (A.colength j) := hc.projective_colength j
   117	  exact Module.Invertible.projective_trans (A := A.colength j)
   118	
   119	end AffAdaptation
   120	
   121	end AlgebraicGeometry

    11	/-!
    12	# Fibrewise H1 witnesses on the widened divisor carrier
    13	
    14	The chart-typed fibre theorem in `DivisorThetaFibreData.lean` has two geometric inputs:
    15	
    16	* a certified adaptation stays certified after passing to a residue field, so its fibre
    17	  presentation divisor has the certificate degree;
    18	* subtracting that fibre divisor from a sufficiently positive theta window gives a divisor
    19	  with the required Picard class and vanishing `H1`.
    20	
    21	Neither input depends on a chart typing of the adaptation cover.  This file proves both for
    22	`AffAdaptation`, whose pieces are arbitrary affine opens.  The conclusion is deliberately the
    23	geometric witness itself, rather than a hypothesis about a not-yet-constructed widened Cech
    24	engine: it is directly reusable by any right-exactness or classifier construction on the
    25	widened carrier and introduces no new premise.

    30	  a widened certified adaptation has the certificate degree.

    32	  explicit divisor `N(a) - d_p` has the transported theta-minus-family class and vanishing
    33	  `H1` once `a` is in the existing high window.

    35	  finite chart presentation of the same local equations has surjective high-window evaluation;

   102	    Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : Int) := by
   103	  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle C K).hom := instIsProperSndLeft C K
   104	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle C K).hom :=
   105	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft C K
   106	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle C K).hom :=
   107	    instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C K
   108	  have h1 : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K)
   109	      = 1 - (genus (baseChangeBundle C K) : Int) := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle C K)
   110	  have h2 : genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C := genus_baseField C K
   111	  have h3 : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genus C : Int) := chi_moduleKSheaf C
   112	  have h4 : (genus C : Int) = (g : Int) := by rw [h3] at hchi; linarith
   113	  rw [h1, h2, h4]
   114	
   115	private lemma picClass_neg_aff {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
   116	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
   117	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   118	    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   119	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (-D) = (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K D)⁻¹ := by
   120	  have h := Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add K (-D) D
   121	  rw [neg_add_cancel, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero] at h
   122	  exact eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_left h.symm

   124	namespace AffAdaptation
   125	
   126	/-- The divisor cut on a field-valued fibre by a widened certified adaptation has exactly the
   127	certificate degree.  Properness makes the intersections of the affine pieces affine, so the
   128	widened certificate base-change theorem applies without an extra overlap hypothesis. -/
   129	theorem IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor_pulledEquations
   130	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   131	    [Algebra R K] [IsScalarTower k R K]
   132	    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   133	    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {n : Nat} (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
   134	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
   135	      ((A.pulledEquations K hc.projective_colength).presentation)) = (n : Int) := by
   136	  have h := (A.pullback K hc.projective_colength).deg_presentationDivisor
   137	  rwa [(A.isCertified_pullback K D.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper hc).finrank_glued] at h
   138	
   139	/-- At every field-valued point of the base, a widened certified family supplies the actual
   140	high-window cohomology witness: `N(a) - d_p` represents the pullback of
   141	`[Theta^a] * [d]^-1` and has vanishing `H1`.  This is the geometric producer needed by the
   142	widened right-exactness/classifier layer; no chart typing of the adaptation cover occurs. -/
   143	theorem IsCertified.fibrewise_thetaSub_h1_witness
   144	    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   145	    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : Nat} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
   146	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   147	    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
   148	    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : Int))
   149	    {a : Nat} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi (relThetaCocycle C k pi a)).H1)
   150	    (hMa : windowM_choice pi hpi g ≤ a)
   151	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   152	    ∃ W : (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).CurveDivisor,
   153	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass p.asIdeal.ResidueField W
   154	          = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   155	              ((thetaChartDatum C R pi a).cechPicClass * d.picClass⁻¹)
   156	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   157	            ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).divisorSheaf
   158	              p.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1) := by
   159	  let K := p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   160	  let dp := Scheme.presentationDivisor K
   161	    ((A.pulledEquations K hc.projective_colength).presentation)
   162	  refine ⟨windowTransportDivisor C K pi a - dp, ?_, ?_⟩
   163	  · have e1 : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K dp
   164	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K) d.picClass := by
   165	      dsimp [dp]
   166	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor,
   167	        Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
   168	      exact A.picClass_pulledEquations K hc.projective_colength
   169	    have e2 : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (windowTransportDivisor C K pi a)
   170	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K)
   171	            ((thetaChartDatum C R pi a).cechPicClass) :=
   172	      (picClass_windowTransportDivisor C K pi a).trans
   173	        (cechPicClass_map_thetaChartDatum C R pi a K).symm
   174	    calc Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (windowTransportDivisor C K pi a - dp)
   175	        = Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (windowTransportDivisor C K pi a)
   176	            * (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K dp)⁻¹ := by
   177	          rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, picClass_neg_aff]
   178	      _ = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K)
   179	            ((thetaChartDatum C R pi a).cechPicClass * d.picClass⁻¹) := by
   180	          rw [e1, e2, map_mul, map_inv]
   181	  · refine subsingleton_h1_windowTransportDivisor_sub C pi hpi K g a
   182	      ha1 hMa hO hchi (chi_relCurve_of_chi_aff C g hchi K) dp ?_
   183	    have hdeg := hc.deg_presentationDivisor_pulledEquations
   184	      (C := C) (R := R) (K := K)
   185	    dsimp [dp] at hdeg ⊢
   186	    rw [hdeg]
   187	    have := Int.natCast_nonneg g
   188	    linarith
   189	
   190	/-- The widened fibre witnesses fire the existing right-exactness engine on an auxiliary finite
   191	chart presentation of the same local-equation system.  Such a presentation exists for every
   192	`d`; it is neither an input nor required to be certified.  Its theta-ideal datum has the
   193	intrinsic class `[Theta^a] * [d]^-1`, so the widened witness supplies exactly the residue-field
   194	divisor and `H1` vanishing that `thetaGluedEval_surjective_of_fibre_witness` consumes.
   195	
   196	This is the chart-free right-exactness bridge at the cover-independent window: the resulting
   197	evaluation has kernel `d.vanishingSubmodule`, hence its window carve has kernel
   198	`divisorWindow d ha1`, while the original widened certificate is used only to produce the
   199	fibre witnesses. -/
   200	theorem IsCertified.exists_chartAdaptation_thetaGluedEval_surjective
   201	    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   202	    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : Nat} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
   203	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   204	    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
   205	    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : Int))
   206	    {a : Nat} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi (relThetaCocycle C k pi a)).H1)
   207	    (hMa : windowM_choice pi hpi g ≤ a) :
   208	    ∃ B : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d, Function.Surjective (B.thetaGluedEval a) := by
   209	  obtain ⟨B⟩ := exists_divisorAdaptation C R pi d
   210	  refine ⟨B, B.thetaGluedEval_surjective_of_fibre_witness hpi (fun p => ?_)⟩
   211	  obtain ⟨W, hWclass, hWH1⟩ :=
   212	    hc.fibrewise_thetaSub_h1_witness C R pi hpi hO hchi ha1 hMa p
   213	  refine ⟨W, ?_, hWH1⟩
   214	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange,
   215	    B.cechPicClass_thetaIdealDatum]
   216	  exact hWclass
   217	
   218	/-- The cover-independent widened window quotient therefore has a finite chart presentation:
   219	it is linearly equivalent to the theta-twisted colength module of an extracted adaptation.
   220	No certificate is transported to that adaptation (which would contradict the strict R2
   221	examples); only the intrinsic local equations and the right-exactness witness are used. -/
   222	theorem IsCertified.exists_chartAdaptation_windowQuotEquiv
   223	    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   224	    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : Nat} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
   225	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   226	    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
   227	    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : Int))
   228	    {a : Nat} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi (relThetaCocycle C k pi a)).H1)
   229	    (hMa : windowM_choice pi hpi g ≤ a) :
   230	    ∃ B : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d,
   231	      Nonempty (((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) ⧸
   232	          divisorWindow d ha1) ≃ₗ[R] B.ThetaGlued a) := by
   233	  obtain ⟨B, hsurj⟩ := hc.exists_chartAdaptation_thetaGluedEval_surjective
   234	    C R pi hpi hO hchi ha1 hMa
   235	  exact ⟨B, ⟨windowQuotEquiv B ha1 hsurj⟩⟩
   236

     9	/-!
    10	# DD-4 (Task 4, (c2)-transport) — `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` as an invertible module over the equalizer
    11	algebra
    12	
    13	The certificate transport for the Θ-twisted glued colength module (`informal` route of
    14	inbox I-0192): there is **no** global isomorphism `W(d)^{Θᵃ} ≅ W(d)` (the twisted delta
    15	is not an automorphism composed with the untwisted one), but both are modules over the
    16	**equalizer algebra** `A_D = W(d)` — the untwisted glued module with its ring structure
    17	— and `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is an *invertible* `A_D`-module once the twisting cocycle pairs
    18	against its inverse (`IsThetaPaired`, the affine-colength-scheme trivialization input).
    19	Under that pairing input, the certificate clause (c2) transports across the twist by
    20	the semilocal Pic-vanishing (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.InvertibleModuleTransfer`).
    21	
    22	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubalgebra` — `A_D`: the glued equalizer as an `R`-subalgebra
    23	  of the chart product (the overlap-restriction arrows are algebra maps).
    24	* `DivisorAdaptation.unitGluedSubmodule` — the `u`-twisted glued module for an arbitrary
    25	  unit family `u` on the piece overlaps; `= gluedSubmodule` at `u = 1`
    26	  (`unitGluedSubmodule_one`), `= thetaGluedSubmodule a` at `u = thetaOvlUnit a`
    27	  (definitionally); componentwise products multiply the twists
    28	  (`mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule`).
    29	* `DivisorAdaptation.thetaSpan`/`thetaInvSpan` — `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` and `W(d)^{Θ⁻ᵃ}` as
    30	  `A_D`-submodules of the chart product.
    31	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsThetaPaired` — **the pairing input**: `Θᵃ`-sections and
    32	  `Θ⁻ᵃ`-sections of the colength scheme pair onto `1` (`thetaSpan * thetaInvSpan = 1`;
    33	  the containment `≤ 1` is automatic, `thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one`).  This is the
    34	  H⁰-trivialization content of the affine colength scheme — the honest cohomological
    35	  residue of the (c2)-transport, discharged by the follow-on brick.
    36	* `DivisorAdaptation.finite_thetaGlued` / `projective_thetaGlued` /
    37	  `rankAtStalk_thetaGlued` — **the (c2)-transport keystones**: given `IsThetaPaired` and
    38	  the certificate, `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is finite projective over `R` of constant rank `n` —
    39	  exactly the inputs `divisorWindowGr` consumes
    40	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyWindow`).
    41	* `DivisorAdaptation.thetaSectionFst`/`thetaSectionSnd` — the two manufactured global
    42	  sections `σ = (t₀ᵃ, 1)`, `τ = (1, t₁ᵃ)` of `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` (the chart coordinates through
    43	  the pinned trivializations), jointly unit-componented; a pairing witness against them
    44	  suffices (`isThetaPaired_of_sectionWitness`).
    45	-/

    72	/-! ## The equalizer algebra `A_D` -/
    73	
    74	/-- **The equalizer algebra `A_D`**: the glued colength module `W(d)` is an
    75	`R`-subalgebra of the chart product — the overlap-restriction arrows are `R`-algebra
    76	maps, so the equalizer condition is closed under multiplication. -/
    77	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebra : Subalgebra R A.chartProd where
    78	  carrier := A.gluedSubmodule
    79	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => A.gluedSubmodule.add_mem hx hy
    80	  mul_mem' := by
    81	    intro x y hx hy
    82	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff] at hx hy ⊢
    83	    intro p
    84	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, map_mul, hx p, hy p]
    85	  one_mem' := by
    86	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
    87	    intro p
    88	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one]
    89	  algebraMap_mem' := by
    90	    intro r
    91	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
    92	    intro p
    93	    rw [Pi.algebraMap_apply, Pi.algebraMap_apply, AlgHom.commutes, AlgHom.commutes]
    94	
    95	lemma mem_gluedSubalgebra_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
    96	    x ∈ A.gluedSubalgebra ↔ x ∈ A.gluedSubmodule :=
    97	  Iff.rfl
    98	
    99	/-- The equalizer algebra and the glued module have the same carrier, `R`-linearly. -/
   100	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraEquiv : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra ≃ₗ[R] A.Glued where
   101	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   102	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   103	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   104	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
   105	  left_inv _ := rfl
   106	  right_inv _ := rfl

   108	/-! ## Unit-twisted glued modules -/
   109	
   110	variable (u v : ∀ i j : A.index, Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ)
   111	
   112	/-- The `u`-twisted right overlap arrow for an arbitrary unit family `u` on the piece
   113	overlaps (the `thetaDeltaRight` shape). -/
   114	noncomputable def unitDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   115	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : A.index × A.index =>
   116	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   117	        ((u p.1 p.2 :
   118	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   119	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   120	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   121	
   122	/-- The `u`-twisted glued colength module. -/
   123	noncomputable def unitGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   124	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.unitDeltaRight u)
   125	
   126	/-- The `u`-twisted equalizer description. -/
   127	lemma mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   128	    s ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule u ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
   129	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   130	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   131	            ((u p.1 p.2 :
   132	              Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   133	              Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2))
   134	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   135	  simp only [unitGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   136	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, unitDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   137	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   138	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   139	
   140	/-- At the trivial unit family, the twisted glued module is the glued module. -/
   141	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_one : A.unitGluedSubmodule 1 = A.gluedSubmodule := by
   142	  ext s
   143	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   144	  refine forall_congr' fun p => ?_
   145	  rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, Units.val_one, map_one, one_mul]
   146	
   147	variable (a : ℕ)
   148	
   149	/-- At the theta unit family, the twisted glued module is `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`. -/
   150	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_thetaOvlUnit :
   151	    A.unitGluedSubmodule (A.thetaOvlUnit a) = A.thetaGluedSubmodule a :=
   152	  rfl

   154	variable {u v}
   155	
   156	/-- **Twists multiply**: the componentwise product of a `u`-twisted and a `v`-twisted
   157	glued family is `(u * v)`-twisted. -/
   158	theorem mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule {s t : A.chartProd}
   159	    (hs : s ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule u) (ht : t ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule v) :
   160	    s * t ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (u * v) := by
   161	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff] at hs ht ⊢
   162	  intro p
   163	  have h1 : (s * t) p.1 = s p.1 * t p.1 := rfl
   164	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl
   165	  have h3 : (((u * v) p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   166	      Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2))
   167	      = ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   168	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2))
   169	        * ((v p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   170	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)) := rfl
   171	  rw [h1, h2, h3, map_mul, map_mul, map_mul, hs p, ht p]
   172	  ring
   173	
   174	variable (u) in
   175	/-- The `u`-twisted glued module as a module over the equalizer algebra `A_D`
   176	(componentwise multiplication by an untwisted family preserves the `u`-twisted
   177	matching). -/
   178	noncomputable def unitGluedOver : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd where
   179	  carrier := A.unitGluedSubmodule u
   180	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => (A.unitGluedSubmodule u).add_mem hx hy
   181	  zero_mem' := (A.unitGluedSubmodule u).zero_mem
   182	  smul_mem' := by
   183	    intro c x hx
   184	    have hc : (c : A.chartProd) ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule 1 := by
   185	      rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]
   186	      exact c.2
   187	    have hmul := A.mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule hc hx
   188	    rw [one_mul] at hmul
   189	    have hsmul : c • x = (c : A.chartProd) * x := Algebra.smul_def c x
   190	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, hsmul]
   191	    exact hmul
   192	
   193	lemma mem_unitGluedOver_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   194	    x ∈ A.unitGluedOver u ↔ x ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule u :=
   195	  Iff.rfl

   197	/-! ## The pairing input and invertibility -/
   198	
   199	/-- `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` as an `A_D`-submodule of the chart product. -/
   200	noncomputable def thetaSpan : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd :=
   201	  A.unitGluedOver (A.thetaOvlUnit a)
   202	
   203	/-- `W(d)^{Θ⁻ᵃ}` (the inverse-twisted glued module) as an `A_D`-submodule. -/
   204	noncomputable def thetaInvSpan : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd :=
   205	  A.unitGluedOver (A.thetaOvlUnit a)⁻¹
   206	
   207	lemma mem_thetaSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   208	    x ∈ A.thetaSpan a ↔ x ∈ A.thetaGluedSubmodule a :=
   209	  Iff.rfl
   210	
   211	lemma mem_thetaInvSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   212	    x ∈ A.thetaInvSpan a ↔ x ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (A.thetaOvlUnit a)⁻¹ :=
   213	  Iff.rfl
   214	
   215	/-- Products of `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-sections are untwisted: the pairing lands in the
   216	equalizer algebra. -/
   217	theorem thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one :
   218	    A.thetaSpan a * A.thetaInvSpan a ≤ 1 := by
   219	  rw [Submodule.mul_le]
   220	  intro s hs t ht

    17	> cert-r2's producer reach U2". **The first clause is true; the second is refuted, in Lean, in
    18	> this file.** Every declaration here is indexed by a `ChartTyping C R π D`, and a cover with a
    19	> straddling piece admits *none* — which is exactly the case protection `I-0492`'s widening
    20	> exists to handle. So on those divisors every theorem below is vacuous, and the tree's only
    21	> `ChartTyping` producer is the migration *from* the old chart-typed carrier. Refutation and its
    22	> consequences: `isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling`; reviewer items `I-0779`/`I-0782`.

    25	> `AffAdaptation` (measurements below, independently confirmed as `I-0780`), it ports cleanly, and
    26	> it is now available for any cover that *does* carry a chart typing.

    28	Protection `I-0492` widened the certificate carrier to arbitrary affine opens, and the
    29	widened lane now produces a class from geometry

    31	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffSeedGate.lean`).  That producer still cannot feed U2, and the
    32	reason recorded across five sessions — "U2 needs a certificate" — is **not** it.  The
    33	argument below correctly identifies the *absence*; where it overreaches is in treating
    34	supplying that absence as sufficient.

    36	## The measurement that renames the seam
    37	
    38	U2's consumer `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean:121`)
    39	quantifies over `DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) π g`, the *chart-typed* value.  There is no
    40	map `DivFamZarAff → DivFamZar` and there cannot be (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2:
    41	a straddling divisor has no chart-typed certificate).  So the only usable route is to
    42	re-derive the ε-value facts on the widened carrier — and *that* is where the absence is:
    43	
    44	> `divFamEps_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivQuot.lean`) needs projectivity and
    45	> constant rank `g` of the **window quotient**.  On `DivFam` those are landed
    46	> *unconditionally* (`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:106`/`:117`) — but their only proof
    47	> route is `windowQuotEquiv` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:179`), whose target is
    48	> `A.ThetaGlued a`, and `ThetaGlued` / `thetaGluedEval` / `thetaOvlUnit` /
    49	> `thetaDeltaRight` / `ker_thetaGluedEval` are defined **only** on `DivisorAdaptation`
    50	> (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean`).

    52	Cross-measured at HEAD: of the files mentioning `AffAdaptation`, **zero** define any theta
    53	arrow.  `DivisorFamilyAffFraming.lean` is right that the ε-pair *statement* is
    54	carrier-indifferent (both carriers have the same `eqns` field and `divisorWindow` reads

    57	## Why this is a port and not new mathematics
    58	
    59	The Θ-layer's chart-dependence is exactly **one `Bool` per piece**.  `FinCoverData`'s
    60	version reads it off the `Sum` index (`pieces_inl_le` / `pieces_inr_le`), which is why it
    61	looks chart-typed; but the side-uniform API it could have used already exists and is
    62	consumed by some sixty files:
    63	
    64	* `relThetaResSide` (`Picard/DivSchemeFamilySide.lean:155`) — the side component,
    65	  restricted into any open below `relPinnedChart (side j)`;
    66	* `relThetaSideUnit` (`:180`) — the matching unit of an ordered pair of sides, whose
    67	  four-case split *is* `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit`'s;
    68	* `relThetaResSide_matching` (`:194`) and `resHom_relThetaResSide` (`:172`).
    69	
    70	Each needs only `piece ≤ relPinnedChart (side j)` — which is **verbatim** the field
    71	`ChartTyping.piece_le` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:204`), the datum `I-0492`
    72	clause 3 deliberately kept *separate* from the certificate clauses precisely so the
    73	Θ-layer could have it without the certificate demanding it.
    74	
    75	So this file is the missing face, built the way clause 3 intends: the twisting data is
    76	indexed by a `ChartTyping`, and **no certificate clause and no locally-certified predicate
    77	mentions it**.
    78	
    79	## What this file does and does not claim
    80	
    81	It builds the widened Θ-twisted glued module and its evaluation, and proves the kernel
    82	bridge — left exactness, i.e. that the kernel is the *same* cover-independent vanishing
    83	submodule the chart-typed layer produces.  That is the input `windowQuotEquiv`'s widened
    84	analogue needs.
    85	
    86	It does **not** prove surjectivity of the widened evaluation (the right-exactness heart,
    87	`thetaGluedEval_surjective`'s analogue), and it does not produce a widened ε-value
    88	identity: those consume the widened certificate's (c2) clause through a widened
    89	`IsThetaPaired`, which is the next face and is *not* built here.  Read this as "the

   144	/-! ## The twisting unit, read off a chart typing
   145	
   146	`FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:149`) splits on the `Sum`
   147	index and produces `1`, the cocycle, or its inverse.  That is `relThetaSideUnit` at the two

   153	lemma pinnedChartOfSide_eq (b : Bool) :

   170	of the two assigned sides, restricted to the overlap.  This replaces
   171	`FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit`'s four-case `Sum` split by one application of
   172	`relThetaSideUnit` — the cases are the same cases, and the `Bool`s now come from the
   173	separate `ChartTyping` datum rather than from the index type. -/
   174	noncomputable def thetaOvlUnit (i j : D.index) :

   176	  relThetaSideUnit a (τ.side i) (τ.side j) (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j)

   178	/-- **The side matching unit at exponent `0` is trivial**, for any pair of sides.  The

   182	The split is over *variable* `Bool`s here (not over `τ.side j` at a use site), which is what

   189	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 false true hW
   190	        = (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hW (relThetaCocycle C R π 0) from rfl,
   191	      relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   192	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 true false hW
   193	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict
   194	            (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
   195	            (relThetaCocycle C R π 0))⁻¹ from rfl,
   196	      relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one, inv_one]
   197	  · rfl

   494	/-- **The widened manufactured section at side `b`**: on each piece, the coordinate power of

   630	/-- **NO `ChartTyping` EXISTS ON A COVER WITH A STRADDLING PIECE.**  If one piece contains a
   631	point outside `V₀` *and* a point outside `V₁`, then `ChartTyping C R π D` is empty: the piece is
   632	assigned some side, `piece_le` puts the *whole* piece inside that pinned chart, and each witness
   633	contradicts one of the two options.
   634	
   635	**This is the honest limit of the whole module, and it cuts against the headline.**  The claim
   636	this file was built on is that the widened carrier lacked a Θ-layer and that supplying it lets
   637	cert-r2's producer reach U2.  The first half stands (see the module docstring's measurements,
   638	independently confirmed as `I-0780`).  The second half does **not**: cert-r2's producer runs
   639	through a cover in which the support sits inside **one** piece `W`
   640	(`exists_affCoverData_swallowedBy`), while the straddling hypotheses of
   641	`forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean:127`) say precisely
   642	that the support has a point outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁` — and both then lie in `W`.
   643	So on exactly the divisors protection `I-0492`'s widening exists to handle, this file's index
   644	type is uninhabited and every theorem in it is vacuous.
   645	
   646	**Compounding it** (`I-0782`): the tree's only producer of a `ChartTyping` is
   647	`FinCoverData.toChartTyping` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:255`), the migration *from* the
   648	old chart-typed carrier. So every instantiation available today factors through `FinCoverData`,
   649	i.e. this layer currently computes on the covers the chart-typed layer already handled,
   650	re-indexed.
   651	
   652	**What the module docstring got wrong, and it is a real methodological error.** `I-0492` clause 3
   653	keeps `ChartTyping` separate from the certificate clauses so that a certificate never *requires*
   654	a chart typing. That is a statement about what is **permitted**, and I read it as evidence about
   655	what is **inhabited**. Those are different questions, and only the second one decides whether a
   656	layer indexed by that datum is usable. The recorded shape is `isolating-a-residue-as-a-class`:
   657	check inhabitation of an index before pricing anything stated over it. -/
   658	theorem isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling (D : AffCoverData C R) (j : D.index)
   659	    {x y : relCurve C R} (hxj : x ∈ D.pieces j) (hyj : y ∈ D.pieces j)
   660	    (hx₀ : x ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
   661	    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
   662	    IsEmpty (ChartTyping C R π D) := by
   663	  refine ⟨fun τ => ?_⟩
   664	  have h := piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ j
   665	  cases hb : τ.side j with
   666	  | false => rw [hb] at h; exact hx₀ (h hxj)
   667	  | true => rw [hb] at h; exact hy₁ (h hyj)
   668	
   669	end Emptiness

    11	/-!
    12	# Invertible modules over a finite algebra: transfer to the base ring (DD-4 (c2)-transport)
    13	
    14	Pure commutative algebra, no schemes (the D1 module-algebra discipline): let `A` be an
    15	`R`-algebra that is finite projective as an `R`-module, and let `M` be an **invertible**
    16	`A`-module (`Module.Invertible`, mathlib's Picard-group vocabulary).  Then `M` is finite
    17	projective over `R` **of the same rank as `A` at every prime**:
    18	
    19	* `Module.Projective.trans` — projectivity descends along a projective algebra: if `A`
    20	  is projective over `R` and `P` projective over `A`, then `P` is projective over `R`
    21	  (the projective mirror of `Module.Projective.of_free_algebra` in
    22	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`).
    23	* `TensorProduct.baseChangeAlgebraModule` — the base-change collapse
    24	  `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` for an `A`-module `M` (the `A`-algebra structure
    25	  on `S ⊗[R] A` through `Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra`).
    26	* `Module.Invertible.finite_trans` / `Module.Invertible.projective_trans` — the
    27	  finiteness/projectivity transfers.
    28	* `Module.Invertible.rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite` — **the rank transfer**: at every
    29	  prime `p` of `R`, `rankAtStalk M p = rankAtStalk A p`.  Route (the semilocal
    30	  Pic-vanishing): the fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` is a finite algebra over the residue
    31	  field, hence artinian, hence semilocal, so its Picard group is trivial (mathlib) and
    32	  the fibre of `M` — an invertible module over the fibre algebra — is **free of rank
    33	  one**; taking `κ(p)`-dimensions gives the claim through `Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.
    34	
    35	The DD-4 consumer instantiates this at `A := ` the glued equalizer algebra of a certified
    36	divisor family (with `Module.Finite`/`Projective`/`rankAtStalk = g` from the certificate
    37	clause (c2)) and `M := ` the Θ-twisted glued module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`
    38	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyThetaRank`).
    39	-/

    49	/-- **Projectivity is transitive**: if `A` is a projective `R`-module and `P` is a
    50	projective `A`-module, then `P` is projective as an `R`-module.  The `A`-splitting
    51	`P →ₗ[A] (P →₀ A)` provided by `Module.projective_def'` restricts to an `R`-splitting,
    52	and `P →₀ A` is a projective `R`-module (a direct sum of copies of `A`, through
    53	`finsuppLequivDFinsupp`). -/
    54	theorem Module.Projective.trans {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A]
    55	    [Algebra R A] {P : Type*} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module A P] [Module R P]
    56	    [IsScalarTower R A P] [Module.Projective R A] [Module.Projective A P] :
    57	    Module.Projective R P := by
    58	  classical
    59	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_def'.mp ‹Module.Projective A P›
    60	  haveI : Module.Projective R (P →₀ A) :=
    61	    Module.Projective.of_equiv (finsuppLequivDFinsupp (R := R) (M := A) (ι := P)).symm
    62	  exact Module.Projective.of_split
    63	    (LinearMap.restrictScalars R s)
    64	    (LinearMap.restrictScalars R (Finsupp.linearCombination A _root_.id))
    65	    (LinearMap.ext fun p => DFunLike.congr_fun hs p)

    67	/-! ## The base-change collapse `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` -/

    69	namespace TensorProduct
