    71	attribute [local instance] Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    72	
    73	section BaseChangeAlgebraModule
    74	
    75	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    76	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    77	variable (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
    78	
    79	/-- The `S`-linear structure map `M →ₗ[R] (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M`, `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`. -/
    80	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit : M →ₗ[R] (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M :=
    81	  LinearMap.restrictScalars R (TensorProduct.mk A (S ⊗[R] A) M 1)
    82	
    83	@[simp]
    84	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply (m : M) :
    85	    baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit S A M m = (1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] m := rfl
    86	
    87	/-- (Implementation) The collapse pairing `(S ⊗[R] A) →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] M`,
    88	`(s ⊗ a, m) ↦ s ⊗ (a • m)`, obtained by currying the composite of the associator with
    89	the `A`-action collapse on the right factor. -/
    90	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing :
    91	    (S ⊗[R] A) →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] M :=
    92	  TensorProduct.curry
    93	    ((LinearMap.lTensor S
    94	        ((LinearMap.liftBaseChange A (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M)).restrictScalars R)) ∘ₗ
    95	      (TensorProduct.assoc R S A M).toLinearMap)
    96	
    97	@[simp]
    98	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul (s : S) (a : A) (m : M) :
    99	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (s ⊗ₜ[R] a) m = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m) := by
   100	  simp [baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing]
   101	
   102	/-- The `A`-action on `S ⊗[R] A` through `Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra`, on pure
   103	tensors. -/
   104	lemma rightAlgebra_smul_tmul (a : A) (s : S) (b : A) :
   105	    a • (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a * b) := by
   106	  change ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a) * (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a * b)
   107	  rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
   108	
   109	/-- (Implementation) The pairing is `A`-balanced. -/
   110	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul (a : A) (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   111	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (a • x) m
   112	      = baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x (a • m) := by
   113	  induction x with
   114	  | zero => simp
   115	  | tmul s b =>
   116	      rw [rightAlgebra_smul_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul,
   117	        baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, mul_smul, smul_comm]
   118	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hx, hy, map_add,
   119	      LinearMap.add_apply]
   120	
   121	/-- (Implementation) The pairing is `S`-semilinear in the first slot. -/
   122	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul_left (c : S) (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   123	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (c • x) m
   124	      = c • baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m := by
   125	  induction x with
   126	  | zero => simp
   127	  | tmul s b =>
   128	      rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul,
   129	        baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul]
   130	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hx, hy, map_add,
   131	      LinearMap.add_apply, smul_add]
   132	
   133	/-- (Implementation) The additive collapse `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M →+ S ⊗[R] M`. -/
   134	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse :
   135	    (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M →+ S ⊗[R] M :=
   136	  TensorProduct.liftAddHom
   137	    { toFun := fun x =>
   138	        { toFun := fun m => baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m
   139	          map_zero' := by simp
   140	          map_add' := fun m n => by simp }
   141	      map_zero' := by ext m; simp
   142	      map_add' := fun x y => by ext m; simp }
   143	    (fun a x m => baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul S A M a x m)
   144	
   145	@[simp]
   146	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   147	    baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M (x ⊗ₜ[A] m)
   148	      = baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- **The base-change collapse**: for an `A`-module `M` and an `R`-algebra `S`, the
   151	base change of `M` along `A → S ⊗[R] A` is the base change along `R → S`,
   152	`S`-linearly: `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` on generators
   153	`(s ⊗ a) ⊗ m ↦ s ⊗ (a • m)`. -/
   154	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModule : (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M where
   155	  toFun := baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M
   156	  map_add' := map_add _
   157	  map_smul' := by
   158	    intro c z
   159	    rw [RingHom.id_apply]
   160	    induction z with
   161	    | zero => simp
   162	    | tmul x m =>
   163	        rw [show c • (x ⊗ₜ[A] m) = (c • x) ⊗ₜ[A] m from TensorProduct.smul_tmul' c x m,
   164	          baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul,
   165	          baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul_left]
   166	    | add z w hz hw =>
   167	        rw [smul_add, map_add, map_add, hz, hw, smul_add]
   168	  invFun := LinearMap.liftBaseChange S (baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit S A M)
   169	  left_inv := by
   170	    intro z
   171	    induction z with
   172	    | zero => simp
   173	    | tmul x m =>
   174	        rw [baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul]
   175	        induction x with
   176	        | zero => simp [TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
   177	        | tmul s b =>
   178	            rw [baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul,
   179	              baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply]
   180	            calc s • ((1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] (b • m))
   181	                = s • (b • ((1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] m)) := by
   182	                  rw [TensorProduct.tmul_smul]
   183	              _ = s • ((b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by
   184	                  rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul' b _ m]
   185	              _ = (s • b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m := TensorProduct.smul_tmul' s _ m
   186	              _ = (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) ⊗ₜ[A] m := by
   187	                  congr 1
   188	                  rw [show b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] (b * 1) from
   189	                    rightAlgebra_smul_tmul S A b 1 1, mul_one, TensorProduct.smul_tmul',
   190	                    smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   191	        | add x y hx hy =>
   192	            rw [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, map_add, hx, hy, TensorProduct.add_tmul]
   193	    | add z w hz hw =>
   194	        rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
   195	  right_inv := by
   196	    intro z
   197	    induction z with
   198	    | zero => simp
   199	    | tmul s m =>
   200	        rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply,
   201	          TensorProduct.smul_tmul' s _ m, baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul,
   202	          show s • (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : A) by
   203	            rw [show (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : A) from rfl,
   204	              TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one],
   205	          baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, one_smul]
   206	    | add z w hz hw => rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
   207	
   208	@[simp]
   209	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModule_tmul_tmul (s : S) (a : A) (m : M) :
   210	    baseChangeAlgebraModule S A M ((s ⊗ₜ[R] a) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m) := by
   211	  change baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M ((s ⊗ₜ[R] a) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m)
   212	  rw [baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul]
   213	
   214	end BaseChangeAlgebraModule

   250	/-- (Implementation) The fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` of a finite `R`-algebra is
   251	semilocal: it is a finite algebra over the residue field, hence artinian. -/
   252	theorem finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   253	    Finite (MaximalSpectrum (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A)) := by
   254	  haveI : IsArtinianRing (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) := by
   255	    haveI : IsArtinian p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) :=
   256	      isArtinian_of_fg_of_artinian'
   257	    exact isArtinian_of_tower p.asIdeal.ResidueField inferInstance
   258	  infer_instance
   259	
   260	/-- **The rank transfer** (the semilocal Pic-vanishing): an invertible module over a
   261	finite projective `R`-algebra `A` has the same rank as `A` at every prime of `R`.
   262	Route: `rankAtStalk` is the fibre dimension (`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`); the fibre
   263	`κ(p) ⊗[R] M ≃ (κ(p) ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M` is an invertible module over the fibre algebra,
   264	which is artinian (hence semilocal), so its Picard group is trivial and the fibre is
   265	free of rank one over the fibre algebra. -/
   266	theorem rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   267	    Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk A p := by
   268	  haveI : Module.Finite R M := finite_trans (A := A)
   269	  haveI : Module.Projective R M := projective_trans (A := A)
   270	  haveI : Module.Flat R M := Module.Flat.of_projective
   271	  haveI : Module.Flat R A := Module.Flat.of_projective
   272	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq, Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   273	  set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   274	  -- the fibre algebra and the fibre of `M` over it
   275	  set Aκ := κ ⊗[R] A with hAκ
   276	  haveI : Finite (MaximalSpectrum Aκ) := finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (A := A) p
   277	  -- the fibre of `M` as a base change over `A`, an invertible `Aκ`-module
   278	  haveI hinv : Module.Invertible Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance
   279	  haveI : Module.Free Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance
   280	  obtain ⟨e⟩ : Nonempty ((Aκ ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[Aκ] Aκ) :=
   281	    Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv.mp ‹_›
   282	  -- transport dimensions along the collapse and the rank-one equivalence
   283	  have h1 : Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] M) = Module.finrank κ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) :=
   284	    (TensorProduct.baseChangeAlgebraModule κ A M).symm.finrank_eq
   285	  have h2 : Module.finrank κ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) = Module.finrank κ Aκ :=
   286	    (e.restrictScalars κ).finrank_eq
   287	  change Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] M) = Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] A)
   288	  rw [h1, h2]
   289	
   290	end Rank

   203	/-- `W(d)^{Θ⁻ᵃ}` (the inverse-twisted glued module) as an `A_D`-submodule. -/
   204	noncomputable def thetaInvSpan : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd :=
   205	  A.unitGluedOver (A.thetaOvlUnit a)⁻¹
   206	
   207	lemma mem_thetaSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   208	    x ∈ A.thetaSpan a ↔ x ∈ A.thetaGluedSubmodule a :=
   209	  Iff.rfl
   210	
   211	lemma mem_thetaInvSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   212	    x ∈ A.thetaInvSpan a ↔ x ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (A.thetaOvlUnit a)⁻¹ :=
   213	  Iff.rfl
   214	
   215	/-- Products of `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-sections are untwisted: the pairing lands in the
   216	equalizer algebra. -/
   217	theorem thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one :
   218	    A.thetaSpan a * A.thetaInvSpan a ≤ 1 := by
   219	  rw [Submodule.mul_le]
   220	  intro s hs t ht
   221	  have hmul := A.mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule
   222	    (A.mem_thetaSpan_iff a |>.mp hs) (A.mem_thetaInvSpan_iff a |>.mp ht)
   223	  rw [mul_inv_cancel, unitGluedSubmodule_one] at hmul
   224	  rw [Submodule.one_eq_range]
   225	  exact ⟨⟨s * t, hmul⟩, rfl⟩
   226	
   227	/-- **The pairing input** (the honest cohomological residue of the (c2)-transport):
   228	the `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-twisted glued modules pair onto the full equalizer algebra — the
   229	trivialization `1 = Σ σₗ · uₗ` of the twist on the affine colength scheme. -/
   230	def IsThetaPaired : Prop :=
   231	  A.thetaSpan a * A.thetaInvSpan a = 1
   232	
   233	/-- The pairing input reduces to hitting `1`. -/
   234	theorem isThetaPaired_of_one_mem
   235	    (h : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ A.thetaSpan a * A.thetaInvSpan a) :
   236	    A.IsThetaPaired a := by
   237	  refine le_antisymm (A.thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one a) ?_
   238	  rw [Submodule.one_eq_span]
   239	  exact Submodule.span_le.mpr (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr h)
   240	
   241	/-- A two-term pairing witness suffices: sections `s, t` of `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` and `u, v` of
   242	`W(d)^{Θ⁻ᵃ}` with `s·u + t·v = 1` discharge the pairing input. -/
   243	theorem isThetaPaired_of_witness {s t u' v' : A.chartProd}
   244	    (hs : s ∈ A.thetaGluedSubmodule a) (ht : t ∈ A.thetaGluedSubmodule a)
   245	    (hu : u' ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (A.thetaOvlUnit a)⁻¹)
   246	    (hv : v' ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (A.thetaOvlUnit a)⁻¹)
   247	    (h : s * u' + t * v' = 1) :
   248	    A.IsThetaPaired a := by
   249	  refine A.isThetaPaired_of_one_mem a ?_
   250	  rw [← h]
   251	  exact Submodule.add_mem _ (Submodule.mul_mem_mul hs hu) (Submodule.mul_mem_mul ht hv)
   252	
   253	/-- **Invertibility of the twisted module over the equalizer algebra**: under the
   254	pairing input, `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is an invertible `A_D`-module (a unit of the submodule
   255	monoid with inverse `W(d)^{Θ⁻ᵃ}`, mathlib's Picard-group vocabulary). -/
   256	theorem invertible_thetaSpan (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) :
   257	    Module.Invertible ↥A.gluedSubalgebra
   258	      ↥(A.thetaSpan a : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd) := by
   259	  haveI hfs : FaithfulSMul ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd := inferInstance
   260	  let I : (Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd)ˣ :=
   261	    ⟨A.thetaSpan a, A.thetaInvSpan a, h, by rw [mul_comm]; exact h⟩
   262	  exact Module.Invertible.left (Submodule.tensorInvEquiv I)
   263	
   264	/-! ## The (c2)-transport keystones -/
   265	
   266	/-- The `A_D`-scalar action on `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`: componentwise multiplication in the chart
   267	product (an untwisted family times a `Θᵃ`-twisted family is `Θᵃ`-twisted). -/
   268	noncomputable instance : SMul ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) where
   269	  smul c x := ⟨(c : A.chartProd) * x, by
   270	    have h := A.mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule (u := 1) (v := A.thetaOvlUnit a)
   271	      (show (c : A.chartProd) ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule 1 by
   272	        rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]; exact c.2)
   273	      (show (x : A.chartProd) ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (A.thetaOvlUnit a) from x.2)
   274	    rw [one_mul] at h
   275	    exact h⟩
   276	
   277	lemma smul_thetaGlued_coe (c : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) (x : A.ThetaGlued a) :
   278	    ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) = (c : A.chartProd) * x :=
   279	  rfl
   280	
   281	/-- **`W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is a module over the equalizer algebra** by componentwise
   282	multiplication. -/
   283	noncomputable instance : Module ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) :=
   284	  Function.Injective.module ↥A.gluedSubalgebra
   285	    ((A.thetaGluedSubmodule a).subtype.toAddMonoidHom) Subtype.val_injective
   286	    (fun c x => by
   287	      change ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) = c • (x : A.chartProd)
   288	      rw [smul_thetaGlued_coe, Algebra.smul_def]
   289	      rfl)
   290	
   291	instance : IsScalarTower R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) where
   292	  smul_assoc r c x := by
   293	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
   294	    have h1 : (((r • c) • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd)
   295	        = ((r • c : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) : A.chartProd) * x := rfl
   296	    have h2 : ((r • (c • x) : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd)
   297	        = r • ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) := rfl
   298	    have h3 : ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) = (c : A.chartProd) * x := rfl
   299	    have h4 : ((r • c : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) : A.chartProd)
   300	        = r • (c : A.chartProd) := rfl
   301	    rw [h1, h2, h3, h4, smul_mul_assoc]
   302	
   303	/-- The twisted `A_D`-submodule and `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` have the same carrier,
   304	`A_D`-linearly. -/
   305	noncomputable def thetaSpanEquiv :
   306	    ↥(A.thetaSpan a : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd)
   307	      ≃ₗ[↥A.gluedSubalgebra] A.ThetaGlued a where
   308	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   309	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   310	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   311	  map_smul' c x := by
   312	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
   313	    rw [smul_thetaGlued_coe]
   314	    change (c • (x : A.chartProd)) = (c : A.chartProd) * x
   315	    rw [Algebra.smul_def]
   316	    rfl
   317	  left_inv _ := rfl
   318	  right_inv _ := rfl
   319	
   320	/-- **Invertibility of `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over the equalizer algebra**, on the consumer's
   321	carrier. -/
   322	theorem invertible_thetaGlued (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) :
   323	    Module.Invertible ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) :=
   324	  haveI := A.invertible_thetaSpan a h
   325	  Module.Invertible.congr (A.thetaSpanEquiv a)
   326	
   327	/-- **(c2)-transport, finiteness**: under the pairing input, the Θ-twisted glued module
   328	is a finite `R`-module. -/
   329	theorem finite_thetaGlued (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) (hfin : Module.Finite R A.Glued) :
   330	    Module.Finite R (A.ThetaGlued a) := by
   331	  haveI := hfin
   332	  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
   333	    Module.Finite.equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
   334	  haveI := A.invertible_thetaGlued a h
   335	  exact Module.Invertible.finite_trans (A := ↥A.gluedSubalgebra)
   336	
   337	/-- **(c2)-transport, projectivity**: under the pairing input, the Θ-twisted glued
   338	module is projective over `R`. -/
   339	theorem projective_thetaGlued (h : A.IsThetaPaired a)
   340	    (hproj : Module.Projective R A.Glued) :
   341	    Module.Projective R (A.ThetaGlued a) := by
   342	  haveI := hproj
   343	  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
   344	    Module.Projective.of_equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
   345	  haveI := A.invertible_thetaGlued a h
   346	  exact Module.Invertible.projective_trans (A := ↥A.gluedSubalgebra)
   347	
   348	/-- **(c2)-transport, constant rank** (the semilocal Pic-vanishing): under the pairing
   349	input and the certificate, the Θ-twisted glued module has the same constant fibre rank
   350	`n` as the untwisted one — the input `divisorWindowGr` consumes. -/
   351	theorem rankAtStalk_thetaGlued {n : ℕ} (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) (hc : A.IsCertified n)
   352	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   353	    Module.rankAtStalk (A.ThetaGlued a) p = n := by
   354	  haveI := hc.finite_glued
   355	  haveI := hc.projective_glued
   356	  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
   357	    Module.Finite.equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
   358	  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
   359	    Module.Projective.of_equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
   360	  haveI := A.invertible_thetaGlued a h
   361	  rw [Module.Invertible.rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite (A := ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) p,
   362	    congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv) p]
   363	  exact hc.rankAtStalk_glued p

     9	/-!
    10	# DD-4 (Task 4, (c2)-transport) — `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` as an invertible module over the equalizer
    11	algebra
    12	
    13	The certificate transport for the Θ-twisted glued colength module (`informal` route of
    14	inbox I-0192): there is **no** global isomorphism `W(d)^{Θᵃ} ≅ W(d)` (the twisted delta
    15	is not an automorphism composed with the untwisted one), but both are modules over the
    16	**equalizer algebra** `A_D = W(d)` — the untwisted glued module with its ring structure
    17	— and `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is an *invertible* `A_D`-module once the twisting cocycle pairs
    18	against its inverse (`IsThetaPaired`, the affine-colength-scheme trivialization input).
    19	Under that pairing input, the certificate clause (c2) transports across the twist by
    20	the semilocal Pic-vanishing (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.InvertibleModuleTransfer`).
    21	
    22	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubalgebra` — `A_D`: the glued equalizer as an `R`-subalgebra
    23	  of the chart product (the overlap-restriction arrows are algebra maps).
    24	* `DivisorAdaptation.unitGluedSubmodule` — the `u`-twisted glued module for an arbitrary
    25	  unit family `u` on the piece overlaps; `= gluedSubmodule` at `u = 1`
    26	  (`unitGluedSubmodule_one`), `= thetaGluedSubmodule a` at `u = thetaOvlUnit a`
    27	  (definitionally); componentwise products multiply the twists
    28	  (`mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule`).
    29	* `DivisorAdaptation.thetaSpan`/`thetaInvSpan` — `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` and `W(d)^{Θ⁻ᵃ}` as
    30	  `A_D`-submodules of the chart product.
    31	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsThetaPaired` — **the pairing input**: `Θᵃ`-sections and
    32	  `Θ⁻ᵃ`-sections of the colength scheme pair onto `1` (`thetaSpan * thetaInvSpan = 1`;
    33	  the containment `≤ 1` is automatic, `thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one`).  This is the
    34	  H⁰-trivialization content of the affine colength scheme — the honest cohomological
    35	  residue of the (c2)-transport, discharged by the follow-on brick.
    36	* `DivisorAdaptation.finite_thetaGlued` / `projective_thetaGlued` /
    37	  `rankAtStalk_thetaGlued` — **the (c2)-transport keystones**: given `IsThetaPaired` and
    38	  the certificate, `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is finite projective over `R` of constant rank `n` —
    39	  exactly the inputs `divisorWindowGr` consumes
    40	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyWindow`).
    41	* `DivisorAdaptation.thetaSectionFst`/`thetaSectionSnd` — the two manufactured global
    42	  sections `σ = (t₀ᵃ, 1)`, `τ = (1, t₁ᵃ)` of `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` (the chart coordinates through
    43	  the pinned trivializations), jointly unit-componented; a pairing witness against them

    74	/-- **The equalizer algebra `A_D`**: the glued colength module `W(d)` is an

    78	  carrier := A.gluedSubmodule
    79	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => A.gluedSubmodule.add_mem hx hy

    82	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff] at hx hy ⊢

    92	    intro p

    99	/-- The equalizer algebra and the glued module have the same carrier, `R`-linearly. -/
   100	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraEquiv : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra ≃ₗ[R] A.Glued where
   101	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   102	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩

   108	/-! ## Unit-twisted glued modules -/

   110	variable (u v : ∀ i j : A.index, Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ)

   112	/-- The `u`-twisted right overlap arrow for an arbitrary unit family `u` on the piece
   113	overlaps (the `thetaDeltaRight` shape). -/
   114	noncomputable def unitDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   115	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : A.index × A.index =>
   116	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   117	        ((u p.1 p.2 :
   118	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :

   156	/-- **Twists multiply**: the componentwise product of a `u`-twisted and a `v`-twisted
   157	glued family is `(u * v)`-twisted. -/
   158	theorem mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule {s t : A.chartProd}
   159	    (hs : s ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule u) (ht : t ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule v) :
   160	    s * t ∈ A.unitGluedSubmodule (u * v) := by
   161	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff] at hs ht ⊢
   162	  intro p
   163	  have h1 : (s * t) p.1 = s p.1 * t p.1 := rfl
   164	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl
   165	  have h3 : (((u * v) p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   166	      Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2))
   167	      = ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   168	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2))
   169	        * ((v p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   170	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces p.1 ⊓ A.pieces p.2)) := rfl
   171	  rw [h1, h2, h3, map_mul, map_mul, map_mul, hs p, ht p]
   172	  ring

   175	/-- The `u`-twisted glued module as a module over the equalizer algebra `A_D`
   176	(componentwise multiplication by an untwisted family preserves the `u`-twisted
   177	matching). -/
   178	noncomputable def unitGluedOver : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd where
   179	  carrier := A.unitGluedSubmodule u

   181	  zero_mem' := (A.unitGluedSubmodule u).zero_mem
   182	  smul_mem' := by
   183	    intro c x hx

   185	      rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]
   186	      exact c.2

   188	    rw [one_mul] at hmul

200	lemma thetaOvlUnit_zero (i j : D.index) : thetaOvlUnit τ 0 i j = 1 :=
   201	  relThetaSideUnit_zero (τ.side i) (τ.side j) (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j)
   202	
   203	/-! ## The Θ-twisted glued colength module -/
   204	
   205	/-- **The Θ-twisted right overlap arrow** over a widened cover: restrict the `p.2`
   206	component to each overlap and multiply by the twisting unit of the pair.  Verbatim
   207	`DivisorAdaptation.thetaDeltaRight` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:203`) with
   208	`thetaOvlUnit` read off `τ`. -/
   209	noncomputable def thetaDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   210	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   211	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   212	        ((thetaOvlUnit τ a p.1 p.2 :
   213	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   214	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   215	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   216	
   217	/-- **The Θ-twisted glued colength module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a widened cover**, spelled as a
   218	kernel so the `FlatCokernel` base-change shapes apply exactly as chart-typed. -/
   219	noncomputable def thetaGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   220	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - thetaDeltaRight A τ a)
   221	
   222	/-- The twisted-equalizer description of the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`. -/
   223	lemma mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   224	    s ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   225	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   226	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   227	            ((thetaOvlUnit τ a p.1 p.2 :
   228	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   229	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   230	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   231	  simp only [thetaGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   232	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, thetaDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   233	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   234	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   235	
   236	/-- The widened Θ-twisted glued colength module, as a type. -/
   237	noncomputable abbrev ThetaGlued : Type u := ↥(thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a)
   238	
   239	/-! ## The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` -/
   240	
   241	/-- **The germ of a widened equation spans the stalk ideal of the family.**  The widened
   242	counterpart of `DivisorAdaptation.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal`
   243	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:322`); its proof is the same one, and it ports because
   244	`eqn_rel` is stated pointwise on both carriers. -/
   245	theorem germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal (j : D.index) {z : relCurve C R}
   246	    (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
   247	    Ideal.span {((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)}
   248	      = d.stalkIdeal z := by
   249	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
   250	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
   251	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   252	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
   253	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
   254	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
   255	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
   256	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   257	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
   258	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
   259	    exact h
   260	  rw [hgerm, Ideal.span_singleton_mul_left_unit (u.isUnit.map
   261	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom)]
   262	  exact d.germ_eqn_span_eq z z (d.cover.mem_opens z)
   263	
   264	/-- The per-piece evaluation of a global theta section: take the side component assigned to
   265	the piece, restrict it, and reduce mod `(f_j)`.  Where the chart-typed version splits on the
   266	`Sum` index (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaPieceEval`), this is one application of
   267	`relThetaResSide` at `τ.side j`. -/
   268	noncomputable def thetaPieceEval (j : D.index) :
   269	    relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] A.colength j :=
   270	  (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
   271	    relThetaResSide a (τ.side j) (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   272	
   273	/-- **The section evaluation into the widened chart product.** -/
   274	noncomputable def thetaEval : relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] A.chartProd :=
   275	  LinearMap.pi (thetaPieceEval A τ a)
   276	
   277	@[simp]
   278	lemma thetaEval_apply (x : relThetaSections C R π a) (j : D.index) :
   279	    thetaEval A τ a x j
   280	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   281	          (relThetaResSide a (τ.side j) (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j) x) := rfl
   282	
   283	/-- The left overlap arrow on a residue class: restrict into the overlap, then reduce.
   284	
   285	Stated here because both widened forms exist only as `private` lemmas of
   286	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCert.lean` (`toOvlLeft_mk'`/`toOvlRight_mk'`) — and both are `rfl`,
   287	so this is a name, not a proof (inbox `I-0712`: `private` hides the name, not the argument).
   288	The `resHom` spelling is the one the matching law below rewrites along. -/
   289	lemma toOvlLeft_mk (i j : D.index) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i)) :
   290	    A.toOvlLeft i j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn i}) s)
   291	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j)
   292	          ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left s) :=
   293	  rfl
   294	
   295	/-- The right overlap arrow on a residue class. -/
   296	lemma toOvlRight_mk (i j : D.index) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)) :
   297	    A.toOvlRight i j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) s)
   298	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j)
   299	          ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right s) :=
   300	  rfl
   301	
   302	/-- **The evaluation lands in the widened Θ-twisted glued module**: on each pairwise
   303	overlap, the global matching of the two side components through the theta cocycle *is* the
   304	Θ-twisted matching of the colengths.
   305	
   306	Where the chart-typed proof (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaEval_mem`) runs a four-case `Sum`
   307	split and calls `relThetaSections_matching` twice with hand-built containments, this is a
   308	single application of `relThetaResSide_matching` — the side-uniform form of the same
   309	matching law.  That collapse is the concrete payoff of taking the sides from a
   310	`ChartTyping` rather than from the index type. -/
   311	theorem thetaEval_mem (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   312	    thetaEval A τ a x ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a := by
   313	  rw [mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff]
   314	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
   315	  rw [thetaEval_apply, thetaEval_apply, toOvlLeft_mk, toOvlRight_mk, ← map_mul]
   316	  refine congrArg _ ?_
   317	  -- both sides restrict the SAME section into the overlap; the side matching law compares
   318	  -- the two assigned sides there, and `thetaOvlUnit` is by definition its unit
   319	  rw [resHom_relThetaResSide (b := τ.side i), resHom_relThetaResSide (b := τ.side j)]
   320	  exact relThetaResSide_matching a (τ.side i) (τ.side j)
   321	    (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j) x
   322	
   323	/-- **The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a widened cover.** -/
   324	noncomputable def thetaGluedEval :
   325	    relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] ThetaGlued A τ a :=
   326	  LinearMap.codRestrict (thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a) (thetaEval A τ a) (thetaEval_mem A τ a)
   327	
   328	lemma thetaGluedEval_coe (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   329	    (thetaGluedEval A τ a x : A.chartProd) = thetaEval A τ a x := rfl
   330	
   331	/-- The kernel of the corestricted evaluation is the kernel of the evaluation. -/
   332	lemma ker_thetaGluedEval_eq_ker :
   333	    LinearMap.ker (thetaGluedEval A τ a) = LinearMap.ker (thetaEval A τ a) :=
   334	  LinearMap.ker_codRestrict _ _ _

   336	/-! ## The equalizer algebra and the unit-twisted glued modules
   337	
   338	Everything in this section is **cover-generic**: it names `D.pieces`, `A.ovlIdeal`,
   339	`A.toOvlLeft/Right` and nothing about a chart, so it ports from
   340	`Picard/DivisorFamilyThetaRank.lean:77-231` with `AffAdaptation` in place of
   341	`DivisorAdaptation` and no other change.  It is the substrate a widened `IsThetaPaired` —
   342	the honest cohomological residue of the (c2)-transport — is stated over. -/
   343	
   344	/-- **The equalizer algebra `A_D` over a widened cover**: the glued colength module is an
   345	`R`-subalgebra of the piece product, because the overlap-restriction arrows are algebra
   346	maps. -/
   347	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebra : Subalgebra R A.chartProd where
   348	  carrier := A.gluedSubmodule
   349	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => A.gluedSubmodule.add_mem hx hy
   350	  mul_mem' := by
   351	    intro x y hx hy
   352	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff] at hx hy ⊢
   353	    intro p
   354	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, map_mul, hx p, hy p]
   355	  one_mem' := by
   356	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   357	    intro p
   358	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one]
   359	  algebraMap_mem' := by
   360	    intro r
   361	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   362	    intro p
   363	    rw [Pi.algebraMap_apply, Pi.algebraMap_apply, AlgHom.commutes, AlgHom.commutes]
   364	
   365	lemma mem_gluedSubalgebra_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   366	    x ∈ gluedSubalgebra A ↔ x ∈ A.gluedSubmodule :=
   367	  Iff.rfl
   368	
   369	/-- The equalizer algebra and the glued module have the same carrier, `R`-linearly. -/
   370	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraEquiv : ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) ≃ₗ[R] A.Glued where
   371	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   372	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   373	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   374	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
   375	  left_inv _ := rfl
   376	  right_inv _ := rfl
   377	
   378	section UnitTwist
   379	
   380	variable (u v : ∀ i j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ)
   381	
   382	/-- The `u`-twisted right overlap arrow for an arbitrary unit family on the piece
   383	overlaps. -/
   384	noncomputable def unitDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   385	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   386	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   387	        ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   388	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   389	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   390	
   391	/-- The `u`-twisted glued colength module. -/
   392	noncomputable def unitGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   393	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - unitDeltaRight A u)
   394	
   395	/-- The `u`-twisted equalizer description. -/
   396	lemma mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   397	    s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   398	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   399	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   400	            ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   401	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   402	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   403	  simp only [unitGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   404	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, unitDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   405	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   406	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   407	
   408	/-- At the trivial unit family, the twisted glued module is the glued module. -/
   409	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_one : unitGluedSubmodule A 1 = A.gluedSubmodule := by
   410	  ext s
   411	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   412	  refine forall_congr' fun p => ?_
   413	  rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, Units.val_one, map_one, one_mul]
   414	
   415	/-- At the Θ unit family, the twisted glued module is the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` — by `rfl`,
   416	exactly as chart-typed, which is what lets the pairing layer be stated over `thetaOvlUnit`
   417	without a transport. -/
   418	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_thetaOvlUnit :
   419	    unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ a) = thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a :=
   420	  rfl
   421	
   422	variable {u v}
   423	
   424	/-- **Twists multiply**: the componentwise product of a `u`-twisted and a `v`-twisted glued
   425	family is `(u * v)`-twisted. -/
   426	theorem mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule {s t : A.chartProd}
   427	    (hs : s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u) (ht : t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A v) :
   428	    s * t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (u * v) := by
   429	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff] at hs ht ⊢
   430	  intro p
   431	  have h1 : (s * t) p.1 = s p.1 * t p.1 := rfl
   432	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl
   433	  have h3 : (((u * v) p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   434	      Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   435	      = ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   436	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   437	        * ((v p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   438	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)) := rfl
   439	  rw [h1, h2, h3, map_mul, map_mul, map_mul, hs p, ht p]
   440	  ring
   441	
   442	variable (u) in
   443	/-- The `u`-twisted glued module as a module over the equalizer algebra `A_D`. -/
   444	noncomputable def unitGluedOver : Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) A.chartProd where
   445	  carrier := unitGluedSubmodule A u
   446	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => (unitGluedSubmodule A u).add_mem hx hy
   447	  zero_mem' := (unitGluedSubmodule A u).zero_mem
   448	  smul_mem' := by
   449	    intro c x hx
   450	    have hc : (c : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A 1 := by
   451	      rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]
   452	      exact c.2
   453	    have hmul := mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule A hc hx
   454	    rw [one_mul] at hmul
   455	    have hsmul : c • x = (c : A.chartProd) * x := Algebra.smul_def c x
   456	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, hsmul]
   457	    exact hmul
   458	
   459	lemma mem_unitGluedOver_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   460	    x ∈ unitGluedOver A u ↔ x ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u :=
   461	  Iff.rfl
   462	
   463	end UnitTwist

   465	/-! ## The manufactured sections, side-uniformly
   466	
   467	`DivisorAdaptation.thetaSectionFst/Snd` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyThetaSections.lean:271/:278`)
   468	are the two sections `σ = (t₀ᵃ; 1)`, `τ = (1; t₁ᵃ)` whose pairing discharges
   469	`IsThetaPaired` chart-typed.  They read the `Sum` index to decide *which side's coordinate
   470	to use on this piece* — and that decision is again a `Bool`, so the side-uniform coordinate
   471	below carries them to the widened cover. -/
   472	
   473	section Sections
   474	
   475	/-- **The side-uniform coordinate power** `t_bᵃ` on the pinned chart of side `b`: `t₀ᵃ` on
   476	`false`, `t₁ᵃ` on `true`.  The `Bool`-indexed form of `relFiberCoordPow` /
   477	`relFiberCoordOnePow`, which the widened sections need for the same reason
   478	`relThetaResSide` was needed for the twisting unit. -/
   479	noncomputable def relFiberCoordSidePow (n : ℕ) : ∀ b : Bool,
   480	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   481	  | false => relFiberCoordPow C R π n
   482	  | true => relFiberCoordOnePow C R π n
   483	
   484	@[simp]
   485	lemma relFiberCoordSidePow_false (n : ℕ) :
   486	    relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) n false
   487	      = relFiberCoordPow C R π n := rfl
   488	
   489	@[simp]
   490	lemma relFiberCoordSidePow_true (n : ℕ) :
   491	    relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) n true
   492	      = relFiberCoordOnePow C R π n := rfl
   493	
   494	/-- **The widened manufactured section at side `b`**: on each piece, the coordinate power of
   495	its *assigned* side when that side is `b`, and `1` otherwise.
   496	
   497	At `b = false` this is `thetaSectionFst` and at `b = true` it is `thetaSectionSnd`, with the
   498	`Sum`-match replaced by a `Bool` comparison against `τ.side j`. -/
   499	noncomputable def thetaSectionSide (b : Bool) : A.chartProd := fun j =>
   500	  if h : τ.side j = b then
   501	    Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   502	      ((relCurve C R).resHom (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   503	        (h ▸ relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) a (τ.side j)))
   504	  else 1
   505	
   506	@[simp]
   507	lemma thetaSectionSide_of_side_eq {b : Bool} {j : D.index} (h : τ.side j = b) :
   508	    thetaSectionSide A τ a b j
   509	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   510	          ((relCurve C R).resHom (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   511	            (h ▸ relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) a (τ.side j))) :=
   512	  dif_pos h
   513	
   514	@[simp]
   515	lemma thetaSectionSide_of_side_ne {b : Bool} {j : D.index} (h : τ.side j ≠ b) :
   516	    thetaSectionSide A τ a b j = 1 :=
   517	  dif_neg h
   518	
   519	end Sections

   521	/-! ## The pairing input, widened
   522	
   523	`IsThetaPaired` is the honest cohomological residue of the (c2)-transport: it is what
   524	`finite/projective/rankAtStalk_thetaGlued` consume, and therefore what a widened
   525	`divisorWindowGr` needs beyond the left-exactness bridge below.  The *statement* and its
   526	automatic half port verbatim; the pairing itself is **not** proved here (chart-typed it is
   527	discharged by manufactured sections through the pinned trivializations, which is where the
   528	two charts genuinely enter). -/
   529	
   530	section Pairing
   531	
   532	/-- The widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` as an `A_D`-submodule. -/
   533	noncomputable def thetaSpan : Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) A.chartProd :=
   534	  unitGluedOver A (thetaOvlUnit τ a)
   535	
   536	/-- The widened inverse-twisted glued module as an `A_D`-submodule. -/
   537	noncomputable def thetaInvSpan : Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) A.chartProd :=
   538	  unitGluedOver A (thetaOvlUnit τ a)⁻¹
   539	
   540	lemma mem_thetaSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   541	    x ∈ thetaSpan A τ a ↔ x ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a :=
   542	  Iff.rfl
   543	
   544	lemma mem_thetaInvSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   545	    x ∈ thetaInvSpan A τ a ↔ x ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ a)⁻¹ :=
   546	  Iff.rfl
   547	
   548	/-- Products of `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-sections are untwisted: the pairing lands in the equalizer
   549	algebra.  This is the automatic half, and it ports verbatim. -/
   550	theorem thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one :
   551	    thetaSpan A τ a * thetaInvSpan A τ a ≤ 1 := by
   552	  rw [Submodule.mul_le]
   553	  intro s hs t ht
   554	  have hmul := mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule A
   555	    (mem_thetaSpan_iff A τ a |>.mp hs) (mem_thetaInvSpan_iff A τ a |>.mp ht)
   556	  rw [mul_inv_cancel, unitGluedSubmodule_one] at hmul
   557	  rw [Submodule.one_eq_range]
   558	  exact ⟨⟨s * t, hmul⟩, rfl⟩
   559	
   560	/-- **The widened pairing input**: the `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-twisted glued modules pair onto the
   561	full equalizer algebra.  Named so the remaining (c2)-transport obligation over the widened
   562	carrier is a *statement in the tree* rather than a gap in prose.
   563	
   564	**This is not proved here, and the reason is precise.** Chart-typed, it is discharged by
   565	`isThetaPaired_of_sectionWitness` from two manufactured global sections `σ = (t₀ᵃ, 1)`,
   566	`τ = (1, t₁ᵃ)` read through the **pinned chart trivializations** — that is where the fixed
   567	pair genuinely enters the Θ-layer, and nothing above needed it.  A widened witness must
   568	produce the analogous sections from the `ChartTyping` instead; whether the per-piece
   569	coordinates suffice is the open question. -/
   570	def IsThetaPaired : Prop :=
   571	  thetaSpan A τ a * thetaInvSpan A τ a = 1
   572	
   573	/-- The widened pairing input reduces to hitting `1`. -/
   574	theorem isThetaPaired_of_one_mem
   575	    (h : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ thetaSpan A τ a * thetaInvSpan A τ a) :
   576	    IsThetaPaired A τ a := by
   577	  refine le_antisymm (thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one A τ a) ?_
   578	  rw [Submodule.one_eq_span]
   579	  exact Submodule.span_le.mpr (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr h)

   147	/-- **The equations are regular** — derived from `eqn_rel` at the point itself, not stored. -/
   148	theorem eqn_regular (j : D.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
   149	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   150	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by

   152	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩

   178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),

   188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))

   190	      intro a ha
   191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha

   193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]

   199	
   200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
   201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
   204	    (by
   205	      intro a ha
   206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
   211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
   213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   214	
   215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
   216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
   217	
   218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
   219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
   220	
   221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
   222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   223	  LinearMap.pi
   224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   225	
   226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
   227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   228	  LinearMap.pi
   229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)

   232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
   233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=

   237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :

   240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
   243	
   244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
   245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule

   250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
   251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
   252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
   253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)

   256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
   257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
   259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued

events.text: The old equalizer proof cannot simply be copied: it represents theta sections as ideals inside the colength ring using pinned-chart trivializations, precisely the structure forbidden by R2. The faithful widened construction must instead glue the intrinsic modules themselves via quasi-coherent restriction isomorphisms. I’m inspecting that API and existing finite-cover descent machinery before deciding the smallest new reusable abstraction.

    12	/-!
    13	# Invertible sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an affine open
    14	
    15	The cocycle pieces used to construct `gluedSheaf` need not contain an arbitrary affine
    16	open.  Nevertheless, every affine open admits a finite basic-open refinement subordinate
    17	to the canonical pointed cover by those pieces.  On each refined basic open the glued
    18	sheaf is free of rank one.  The existing localization-span engine then proves that its
    19	sections on the original affine open are finite projective.
    20	
    21	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.AffineSectionsModel` packages the quasi-coherent action chosen by
    22	that internal refinement together with the finite, projective, and invertible instances.
    23	Returning a `Nonempty` model keeps the refinement choice noncomputable while giving
    24	downstream code a single datum from which it can install all four compatible instances.
    25	
    26	This is the chart-free line-bundle substrate needed to restrict a positive theta twist to
    27	the arbitrary affine pieces of `AffAdaptation`: the divisor cover is not required to lie in
    28	either pinned theta chart.
    29	-/

    44	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    45	
    46	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    47	
    48	/-- A compatible quasi-coherent module structure on the sections of a cocycle-glued
    49	line bundle over an affine open, together with its finite projective rank-one properties.
    50	
    51	The module instance is written explicitly in the fields so that it is definitionally the
    52	one induced by `qcoh`; a consumer may install `M.qcoh` and recover `M.finite` and
    53	`M.projective` without any proof-irrelevance transport. -/
    54	structure AffineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    55	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) where
    56	  qcoh : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V
    57	  finite : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    58	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    59	  projective : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    60	    (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _
    61	    (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    62	  invertible : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    63	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    64	
    65	/-- Sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on every affine open admit a compatible
    66	invertible module model.  The proof chooses a finite basic-open refinement of the canonical
    67	pointed cover, trivializes after the resulting faithfully flat product localization, and
    68	descends invertibility; finiteness and projectivity are recorded on the same action. -/
    69	theorem nonempty_affineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    70	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    71	    Nonempty (D.AffineSectionsModel V) := by
    72	  classical
    73	  obtain ⟨ι, fint, f, anchor, coeff, hP, hpart⟩ :=
    74	    hV.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement D.pointedCover
    75	  letI : Fintype ι := fint
    76	  let sigma : ι → D.index := fun i => D.pieceIndex (anchor i)
    77	  have hP' : ∀ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) ≤ D.pieces (sigma i) := hP
    78	  have hcov : V ≤ ⨆ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) :=
    79	    le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
    80	  let q : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V :=
    81	    gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' hcov
    82	  letI : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V := q
    83	  let m : Module Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) :=
    84	    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := D.sheaf) (le_refl V)
    85	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
    86	    Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
    87	  have hfin : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ _ m :=
    88	    moduleFinite_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
    89	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
    90	  have hproj : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    91	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ m :=
    92	    projective_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
    93	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
    94	  letI pieceBaseModule : ∀ i : ι, Module Γ(relCurve C B, V)
    95	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
    96	    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := D.sheaf) ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i))
    97	  letI pieceModule : ∀ i : ι,
    98	      Module Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
    99	        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
   100	    gluedPieceModule B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' i
   101	  letI pieceTower : ∀ i : ι, IsScalarTower Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   102	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
   103	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
   104	    isScalarTower_chart_piece B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle
   105	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
   106	  letI pieceLocalization : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalization.Away (f i)
   107	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) := fun i =>
   108	    hV.isLocalization_basicOpen (f i)
   109	  haveI pieceLocalized : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i))
   110	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
   111	        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V)) := fun i =>
   112	    isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
   113	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
   114	  let e (i : ι) :
   115	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) ⊗[Γ(relCurve C B, V)]
   116	          (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
   117	        ≃ₗ[Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))]
   118	          Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) :=
   119	    (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange (Submonoid.powers (f i))
   120	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
   121	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
   122	        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V))).equiv.trans
   123	      (gluedPieceEquiv B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' i)
   124	  letI : Module.FaithfullyFlat Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   125	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))) :=
   126	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_of_span_eq_top f hspan
   127	  let E := Module.piTrivialization e
   128	  letI : Module.Invertible
   129	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))
   130	      ((∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))) ⊗[Γ(relCurve C B, V)]
   131	        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))) :=
   132	    Module.Invertible.congr E.symm
   133	  have hinv : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ _ m :=
   134	    Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
   135	      Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   136	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))
   137	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
   138	  exact ⟨⟨q, hfin, hproj, hinv⟩⟩
   139	
   140	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   141	
   142	end AlgebraicGeometry

    14	/-!
    15	# Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules
    16	
    17	Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings.  This file shows that the
    18	module-theoretic properties *finite*, *finitely presented*, *flat*, *projective* and
    19	*invertible* all descend along `A → B`: if `B ⊗[A] P` has the property over `B`, then `P`
    20	has it over `A`.  Combined with the effectivity theorem of
    21	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent` this yields: a `B`-module `M` with a descent
    22	datum descends to an `A`-module `M₀` (unique up to canonical isomorphism), and if `M` is
    23	invertible then so is `M₀`.
    24	
    25	The descent of invertibility is reduced, via the definition
    26	`Module.Invertible R M ↔ Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)`, to two ingredients:
    27	
    28	* the *dual base-change comparison* `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is an
    29	  isomorphism for `P` finite projective (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`, proved by a
    30	  retract argument from the finite free case, which is `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`);
    31	* bijectivity of `A`-linear maps descends along faithfully flat maps
    32	  (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective`).
    33	
    34	Finiteness and projectivity of `P` are themselves obtained by descent: mathlib provides
    35	finiteness (`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`) and flatness
    36	(`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`); we add finite presentation
    37	(`Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`), and
    38	projectivity follows from flat + finitely presented.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`:
    43	  finite presentation descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    44	* `Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: finite projectivity
    45	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    46	* `Module.dualBaseChange A B P : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)`: the dual
    47	  base-change comparison map.
    48	* `Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`: the comparison map is bijective for finite projective
    49	  `P` (over an arbitrary `A`-algebra `B`).
    50	* `Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: invertibility
    51	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    52	* `Module.DescentDatum.finite_descended`, `…flat_descended`,
    53	  `…finitePresentation_descended`, `…projective_descended`,
    54	  `…invertible_descended`: for a descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to a
    55	  faithfully flat `A → B`, the descended module inherits each property from `M`;
    56	  in particular **an invertible module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
    57	  module**.
    58	
    59	All modules live in a single universe `u`.
    60	-/
    61	
    62	universe u
    63	
    64	open TensorProduct
    65	
    66	namespace Module
    67	
    68	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    69	
    70	/-! ### Descent of finite presentation -/
    71	
    72	/-- Finite presentation of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
    73	theorem FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
    74	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    75	    [Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
    76	    Module.FinitePresentation A P := by
    77	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
    78	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
    79	  obtain ⟨n, p, hp⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
    80	  have hpB : Function.Surjective (p.baseChange B) := by
    81	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    82	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B hp
    83	  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)).FG :=
    84	    Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker (p.baseChange B) hpB
    85	  have hexact := Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B p.exact_subtype_ker_map
    86	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B) := by
    87	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    88	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
    89	      (LinearMap.ker p).injective_subtype
    90	  have hrange : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B)
    91	      = LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) := by
    92	    ext x
    93	    rw [LinearMap.mem_range, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    94	    constructor
    95	    · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
    96	      simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    97	      exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
    98	    · intro hx
    99	      rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hx
   100	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact x).mp hx
   101	      exact ⟨y, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]; exact hy⟩
   102	  have e : (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) ≃ₗ[B] LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) :=
   103	    (LinearEquiv.ofInjective _ hinj).trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ hrange)
   104	  have : Module.Finite B (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)) := Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr hker
   105	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) := Module.Finite.equiv e.symm
   106	  have : Module.Finite A (LinearMap.ker p) :=
   107	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   108	  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective p hp (Module.Finite.iff_fg.mp this)
   109	
   110	/-- Finite projectivity of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
   111	theorem Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
   112	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   113	    [Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] P)] [Projective B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
   114	    Projective A P := by
   115	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
   116	    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B (B ⊗[A] P)
   117	  have : Module.FinitePresentation A P :=
   118	    FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
   119	  have : Module.Flat A P := Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A P B
   120	  exact Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation (R := A) (M := P)

   122	/-! ### The dual base-change comparison map -/
   123	
   124	section DualBaseChange
   125	
   126	variable {A B} in
   127	/-- Two `B`-functionals on `B ⊗[A] X` that agree on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ x` are equal. -/
   128	private theorem dual_ext {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
   129	    {F G : Dual B (B ⊗[A] X)} (h : ∀ x : X, F (1 ⊗ₜ x) = G (1 ⊗ₜ x)) : F = G := by
   130	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   131	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
   132	  intro b x
   133	  have hb : b ⊗ₜ[A] x = b • (1 ⊗ₜ[A] x : B ⊗[A] X) := by
   134	    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   135	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, hb, map_smul, h]
   136	
   137	variable (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
   138	
   139	/-- The canonical `B`-linear comparison map from the base change of the dual to the dual
   140	of the base change, `b ⊗ₜ f ↦ b • (f.baseChange B)`.  It is bijective for finite
   141	projective `P` (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`). -/
   142	noncomputable def dualBaseChange : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
   143	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (Module.Dual.baseChange B)
   144	
   145	@[simp] theorem dualBaseChange_tmul (b : B) (f : Dual A P) :
   146	    dualBaseChange A B P (b ⊗ₜ f) = b • Module.Dual.baseChange B f := rfl
   147	
   148	/-- Naturality of the dual base-change comparison map. -/
   149	theorem dualBaseChange_naturality {P Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
   150	    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] (g : P →ₗ[A] Q) :
   151	    dualBaseChange A B P ∘ₗ g.dualMap.baseChange B =
   152	      (g.baseChange B).dualMap ∘ₗ dualBaseChange A B Q := by
   153	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   154	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
   155	  intro b f
   156	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]
   157	  refine dual_ext fun x => ?_
   158	  simp [Module.Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul]
   159	
   160	variable {A B} in
   161	private theorem bijective_dualBaseChange_free (n : ℕ) :
   162	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A)) := by
   163	  have j : IsBaseChange B (TensorProduct.mk A B (Fin n → A) 1) :=
   164	    TensorProduct.isBaseChange A (Fin n → A) B
   165	  have k : IsBaseChange B (Algebra.linearMap A B) := IsBaseChange.linearMap A B
   166	  have hlr : IsBaseChange B (IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B)) :=
   167	    IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight j k
   168	  have heq : Module.Dual.baseChange (R := A) B (V := Fin n → A)
   169	      = IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B) := by
   170	    refine LinearMap.ext fun f => dual_ext fun x => ?_
   171	    have h1 := IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply j (Algebra.linearMap A B) f x
   172	    simpa [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using h1.symm
   173	  have hlift : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) = hlr.equiv.toLinearMap := by
   174	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   175	    apply TensorProduct.ext'
   176	    intro b f
   177	    simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dualBaseChange_tmul,
   178	      IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, heq]
   179	  rw [hlift]
   180	  exact hlr.equiv.bijective
   181	
   182	/-- **The dual commutes with base change for finite projective modules**: the comparison
   183	map `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is bijective when `P` is finite projective. -/
   184	theorem bijective_dualBaseChange [Module.Finite A P] [Projective A P] :
   185	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B P) := by
   186	  obtain ⟨n, r, hr⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
   187	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_lifting_property r LinearMap.id hr
   188	  have hfree := bijective_dualBaseChange_free (A := A) (B := B) n
   189	  have hnat_r := dualBaseChange_naturality A B r
   190	  have hnat_s := dualBaseChange_naturality A B s
   191	  -- the two retraction identities
   192	  have hcomp : s.dualMap ∘ₗ r.dualMap = LinearMap.id := by
   193	    ext f x
   194	    simpa using congrArg f (LinearMap.congr_fun hs x)
   195	  have hu : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] Dual A P,
   196	      s.dualMap.baseChange B (r.dualMap.baseChange B x) = x := by
   197	    intro x
   198	    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hcomp, LinearMap.baseChange_id,
   199	      LinearMap.id_apply]
   200	  have hcompB : (r.baseChange B) ∘ₗ (s.baseChange B) = LinearMap.id := by
   201	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hs, LinearMap.baseChange_id]
   202	  have hv : ∀ y : Dual B (B ⊗[A] P),
   203	      (s.baseChange B).dualMap ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y) = y := by
   204	    intro y
   205	    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.dualMap_comp_dualMap, hcompB, LinearMap.dualMap_id,
   206	      LinearMap.id_apply]
   207	  constructor
   208	  · intro x y hxy
   209	    have h1 : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B x)
   210	        = dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B y) := by
   211	      rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r]
   212	      simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, hxy]
   213	    have h2 := hfree.injective h1
   214	    rw [← hu x, ← hu y, h2]
   215	  · intro y
   216	    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hfree.surjective ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y)
   217	    refine ⟨s.dualMap.baseChange B z, ?_⟩
   218	    have := LinearMap.congr_fun hnat_s z
   219	    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at this
   220	    rw [this, hz, hv]
   221	
   222	end DualBaseChange

   224	/-! ### Descent of invertibility -/
   225	
   226	/-- **Invertibility of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps**: if `A → B` is
   227	faithfully flat and `B ⊗[A] P` is an invertible `B`-module, then `P` is an invertible
   228	`A`-module. -/
   229	theorem Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
   230	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   231	    [Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
   232	    Module.Invertible A P := by
   233	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
   234	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   235	  have hproj : Projective A P :=
   236	    Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
   237	  -- the contraction square: base change of `contractLeft A P` factors through
   238	  -- `contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P)` via the dual base-change comparison map
   239	  have hsquare : (contractLeft A P).baseChange B =
   240	      ((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P) ∘ₗ
   241	          (dualBaseChange A B P).rTensor (B ⊗[A] P)) ∘ₗ
   242	        (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).toLinearMap := by
   243	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   244	    ext f p
   245	    simp only [AlgebraTensorModule.curry_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_self, curry_apply,
   246	      LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, contractLeft_apply,
   247	      LinearMap.restrictScalars_comp, LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
   248	      Function.comp_apply, AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul,
   249	      dualBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.smul_apply, Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul, smul_eq_mul,
   250	      Algebra.mul_smul_comm, mul_one, AlgebraTensorModule.rid_symm_apply]
   251	    rw [← TensorProduct.smul_tmul', ← TensorProduct.tmul_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   252	  have hbij : Function.Bijective ((contractLeft A P).baseChange B) := by
   253	    rw [hsquare]
   254	    simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
   255	    exact (((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.bijective.comp
   256	        (Module.Invertible.bijective (R := B) (M := B ⊗[A] P))).comp
   257	        ((Module.Invertible.rTensor_bijective_iff (M := B ⊗[A] P)).mpr
   258	          (bijective_dualBaseChange A B P))).comp
   259	      (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).bijective
   260	  rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hbij
   261	  exact ⟨(Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective A B _).mp hbij⟩
   262	
   263	/-! ### Properties of the descended module of a descent datum -/
   264	
   265	namespace DescentDatum
   266	
   267	variable {A B} {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
   268	variable (D : DescentDatum A B M) [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   269	
   270	theorem finite_descended [Module.Finite B M] : Module.Finite A D.descended := by
   271	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
   272	  exact Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   273	
   274	theorem flat_descended [Module.Flat B M] : Module.Flat A D.descended := by
   275	  have : Module.Flat B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv D.descentEquiv
   276	  exact Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A D.descended B
   277	
   278	theorem finitePresentation_descended [Module.FinitePresentation B M] :
   279	    Module.FinitePresentation A D.descended := by
   280	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) :=
   281	    Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective D.descentEquiv.symm.toLinearMap
   282	      D.descentEquiv.symm.surjective
   283	      (by simpa using Submodule.fg_bot)
   284	  exact FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B
   285	    D.descended
   286	
   287	theorem projective_descended [Module.Finite B M] [Projective B M] :
   288	    Projective A D.descended := by
   289	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
   290	  have : Projective B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Projective.of_equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
   291	  exact Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended
   292	
   293	/-- **Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules**: if `M` is an invertible `B`-module
   294	with a descent datum relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`, then the descended `A`-module
   295	is invertible.  Together with `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv` (which exhibits
   296	`B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ M`) and `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended` (uniqueness), this is the
   297	descent theorem for the Picard group. -/
   298	theorem invertible_descended [Module.Invertible B M] : Module.Invertible A D.descended := by
   299	  have : Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := .congr D.descentEquiv.symm
   300	  exact Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended
   301	
   302	end DescentDatum
   303	
   304	end Module

     9	/-!
    10	# The transition cocycle of a locally trivialized module, and its Picard class
    11	
    12	Let `A` be a commutative ring, `N` an `A`-module, and `f : ι → A` a finite family with
    13	localization models `S i`, `T i j`, `W i j k` away from the single, double and triple
    14	products as in `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LocalizationCocycle`.  Given trivializations
    15	`e i : S i ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[S i] S i` on the members of the cover, this file:
    16	
    17	* forms the **transition cocycle** `trivializationCocycle e i j : (T i j)ˣ` — the
    18	  transition unit between the two pushforwards of `e i` and `e j` to the overlap — and
    19	  shows it is a Čech cover cocycle (`isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle`), the diagonal
    20	  and cocycle conditions being instances of the transition-unit calculus of
    21	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.BaseChangeTrivialization` plus the uniqueness of `A`-algebra
    22	  maps out of localizations;
    23	* assembles the componentwise trivializations into one over the cover algebra
    24	  `B := ∀ i, S i` (`Module.piTrivialization`);
    25	* proves the **descent identification** (`picClass_trivializationCocycle`): the Picard
    26	  class of the descent cocycle associated with the transition cocycle is the class of
    27	  `N` itself.  The compatibility of the assembled trivialization with the twisted
    28	  descent datum reduces, through the identification `B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∀ p, T p.1 p.2`, to the
    29	  defining property of the transition units, and uniqueness of descent
    30	  (`Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`) identifies the descended module with `N`.
    31	
    32	This is the algebraic heart of the surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism
    33	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_surjective`).
    34	-/
    35	
    36	universe u
    37	
    38	open TensorProduct
    39	
    40	/-! ## Assembling componentwise trivializations over a finite product -/
    41	
    42	namespace Module
    43	
    44	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    45	variable {S : ι → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)]
    46	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    47	
    48	/-- The canonical `A`-linear distribution of a base change over a finite product of
    49	`A`-algebras. -/
    50	noncomputable def piBaseChangeDistrib :
    51	    ((∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[A] ∀ i, S i ⊗[A] N :=
    52	  (TensorProduct.comm A _ _).trans ((TensorProduct.piRight A A N S).trans
    53	    (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ TensorProduct.comm A N (S i)))
    54	
    55	@[simp]
    56	lemma piBaseChangeDistrib_tmul (b : ∀ i, S i) (n : N) :
    57	    piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S) (b ⊗ₜ[A] n) = fun i ↦ b i ⊗ₜ[A] n := by
    58	  funext i
    59	  simp [piBaseChangeDistrib, TensorProduct.piRight_apply]
    60	
    61	variable (e : ∀ i, (S i ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[S i] S i)
    62	
    63	/-- The `A`-linear map underlying `piTrivialization`: `n ↦ (i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n))`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def piTrivializationBase : N →ₗ[A] ∀ i, S i where
    65	  toFun n i := e i (1 ⊗ₜ n)
    66	  map_add' n m := by
    67	    funext i
    68	    simp only [Pi.add_apply, TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add]
    69	  map_smul' a n := by
    70	    funext i
    71	    simp only [RingHom.id_apply, Pi.smul_apply, TensorProduct.tmul_smul]
    72	    exact LinearMapClass.map_smul_of_tower (e i) a _
    73	
    74	/-- Componentwise trivializations of `N` over a finite family of `A`-algebras assemble
    75	into a trivialization over the product algebra, sending `1 ⊗ₜ n` to
    76	`fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n)` (`piTrivialization_one_tmul`). -/
    77	noncomputable def piTrivialization :
    78	    ((∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[∀ i, S i] ∀ i, S i := by
    79	  refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective
    80	    (LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e)) ?_
    81	  have key : ⇑(LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e))
    82	      = (fun v i ↦ e i (v i)) ∘ ⇑(piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S)) := by
    83	    funext x
    84	    induction x with
    85	    | zero => exact funext fun i ↦ by simp
    86	    | tmul b n =>
    87	        funext i
    88	        simp only [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, Function.comp_apply,
    89	          piBaseChangeDistrib_tmul]
    90	        have hb : (b i ⊗ₜ[A] n : S i ⊗[A] N) = b i • ((1 : S i) ⊗ₜ[A] n) := by
    91	          rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    92	        rw [hb, map_smul]
    93	        simp [piTrivializationBase, smul_eq_mul]
    94	    | add x y hx hy =>
    95	        rw [map_add, hx, hy]
    96	        funext i
    97	        simp only [Function.comp_apply, map_add, Pi.add_apply]
    98	  rw [key]
    99	  exact ((Equiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ (e i).toEquiv).bijective).comp
   100	    (piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S)).bijective
   101	
   102	@[simp]
   103	lemma piTrivialization_one_tmul (n : N) :
   104	    piTrivialization e (1 ⊗ₜ n) = fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n) := by
   105	  change LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e) (1 ⊗ₜ n) = _
   106	  rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
   107	  rfl
   108	
   109	end Module
